source_task_text: Break down large conservation efforts into phased implementation plans
rationale: AI PM tools augment; seasonal/regulatory/ecological sequencing requires professional knowledge. P-position foundational learning.

source_task_text: Develop and maintain Gantt charts to track project timelines and dependencies
rationale: ◉ CLD (Moderate). AI PM tools auto-generate Gantt charts from task inputs. Manual timeline construction — a primary mechanism for developing scheduling logic at entry level — substantially compressed. Review-and-certify persists.

source_task_text: Coordinate with cross-functional teams to align fieldwork with seasonal windows
rationale: H: criterion (c). Live cross-team coordination requires real-time reading of competing priorities, field crew constraints, and contractor relationships. The practitioner's relational authority enables alignment that AI cannot mediate without losing the coordination quality.

source_task_text: Prepare project budgets that align with grant or program requirements
rationale: ◉ CLD (High). AI budget template tools and grant compliance checkers eliminate manual budget construction from requirements. Primary mechanism for entry-level financial literacy development substantially compressed to review-and-certify. Highest-severity CLD in 3.1.

source_task_text: Track actual costs against projected expenses and update forecasts
rationale: ◉ CLD (High). Financial management software performs continuous expense tracking and variance analysis. Manual comparison task — primary entry-level financial administration learning pathway — substantially compressed.

source_task_text: Justify budget adjustments based on project scope changes or risks
rationale: AI models adjustment scenarios; justification requires integrated knowledge of funder intent, contractor relationships, and scope negotiation. Institutional accountability act, not computational. T3 planning/synthesis → H2.

source_task_text: Identify risks such as weather delays or regulatory barriers early in project design
rationale: AI risk identification tools assist; judgment about consequential risks for this project's ecological context and regulatory jurisdiction is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Develop risk mitigation strategies and assign risk owners
rationale: Risk mitigation design requires institutional authority and knowledge of organizational risk tolerance and accountability structures. SC governance work. T3 pattern applied at T2 planning function → H2.

source_task_text: Monitor and manage risk mitigation measures during implementation
rationale: AI monitoring tools track risk triggers; interpretation of whether a flagged condition represents the anticipated risk requires contextual judgment. T3 monitoring function → H1.

source_task_text: Develop and execute contracts with contractors and partners
rationale: AI contract drafting tools deployed; contract development for environmental work requires knowledge of site conditions, regulatory constraints, and relationship context.

source_task_text: Monitor contractor performance and compliance against contract terms
rationale: Contract management software performs continuous compliance tracking and performance scoring. Human role: review outputs and adjudicate ambiguous performance situations. C-position Ac: moderate severity.

source_task_text: Negotiate and administer contract amendments and change orders
rationale: H: criterion (a) and (b). Contract negotiation requires the practitioner's relational credibility with contractors. Institutional legitimacy of negotiated amendments depends on who negotiated and under what authority. AI cannot replicate the accountability relationship.

source_task_text: Develop performance metrics and monitoring frameworks for projects
rationale: AI benchmarking assists; selecting which outcomes matter for this project's ecological and social context requires professional judgment. T1 planning/design → H2.

source_task_text: Collect and analyze performance data against project objectives
rationale: ◉ CLD (Moderate). AI project management dashboards aggregate outputs and generate variance analyses automatically. Manual data collection and analysis — entry-level analytical learning pathway — substantially compressed.

source_task_text: Synthesize evaluation findings and recommend project adjustments
rationale: Synthesis requires integrated judgment connecting data patterns to ecological, organizational, and stakeholder realities. AI assists; practitioner synthesizes and recommends. T3 synthesis → H2.

source_task_text: Conduct organizational capacity and SWOT analysis
rationale: AI diagnostic tools assist; judgment about what capacity gaps mean for this organization's mission context is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Synthesize assessment findings and identify strategic gaps
rationale: Synthesis integrating capacity against mission and environmental context requires integrated institutional judgment. T3 pattern: synthesis → H2.

source_task_text: Present organizational assessment to board and leadership for strategic decision-making
rationale: H: criterion (b). Board presentation is an accountability relationship — practitioner's standing and credibility determine whether assessment produces strategic action. AI cannot appear before a board with the same institutional consequence.

source_task_text: Facilitate organizational stakeholder engagement to surface mission priorities
rationale: H: criterion (c). Live facilitation of mission stakeholder engagement requires real-time reading and response to group dynamics. Quality of mission that emerges depends on quality of facilitation in the room.

source_task_text: Draft and iterate organizational vision and mission statements
rationale: AI drafting tools assist; mission statement requires authentic institutional buy-in and synthesis of stakeholder input into language that holds under governance scrutiny.

source_task_text: Secure board adoption of vision and mission through governance process
rationale: H: criterion (b). Board adoption is a governance accountability event — practitioner's institutional authority to bring the recommendation determines the outcome. X-position: senior organizational leaders only. ⚑ Delphi: X vs. C boundary.

source_task_text: Develop SMART objectives aligned with mission and stakeholder priorities
rationale: AI SMART objective tools assist; judgment about which objectives are achievable and strategically meaningful for this organization is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Negotiate goal consensus across program teams and leadership
rationale: H: criterion (a) and (c). Goal negotiation requires relational authority and real-time reading of competing institutional interests and power relationships. AI cannot mediate consensus without losing legitimacy of agreed outcomes.

source_task_text: Document and communicate adopted goals to stakeholders and funders
rationale: ◉ CLD (Low-Moderate). AI communication and drafting tools compress goal documentation and stakeholder communication. Entry-level strategic communication learning pathway reduced.

source_task_text: Develop logic models and theory-of-change frameworks for program strategy
rationale: AI theory-of-change tools assist; strategy design requires integrated knowledge of ecological systems, organizational capacity, and stakeholder landscape. T1 planning → H2.

source_task_text: Identify and sequence implementation priorities and resource requirements
rationale: AI prioritization tools assist; judgment about organizational feasibility and political viability is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Build and maintain implementation partnerships and institutional relationships
rationale: H: criterion (a). The practitioner's relationship with partner organizations is the professional contribution — institutional trust built over time determines whether implementation partnerships are genuine. AI cannot replicate the relationship.

source_task_text: Design monitoring and learning protocols for adaptive management cycles
rationale: ▲ OBAM rule. AI monitoring framework tools assist; defining ecologically meaningful indicators and who holds revision authority are governance and judgment questions. T1 planning → H2.

source_task_text: Facilitate organizational learning reviews and decision gate processes
rationale: H: criterion (b) and (c). ▲ OBAM rule. AM learning reviews are accountability events — who facilitates under what institutional authority determines whether the organization actually revises its approach. Live facilitation of a group confronting disconfirming evidence requires relational trust that AI cannot substitute.

source_task_text: Document adaptive management decisions and revise program plans
rationale: ◉ CLD (Low-Moderate). AI documentation tools compress AM decision record-keeping and plan revision. Documentation alone is not the primary mechanism for developing AM competency, hence low-moderate severity.

source_task_text: Recruit, hire, and onboard program staff against organizational needs
rationale: AI recruiting and screening tools deployed; hiring judgment about organizational culture fit and specific constraint navigation is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Supervise staff performance and provide ongoing feedback and development
rationale: H: criterion (a). The supervisory relationship is itself the professional contribution — the trust and authority enabling genuine feedback cannot be delegated to or replicated by AI. The specific practitioner's accountability to and for specific people is irreducible.

source_task_text: Manage HR documentation, personnel records, and compliance reporting
rationale: ◉ CLD (Moderate). HRIS and AI compliance dashboards substantially compress personnel documentation. Entry-level HR administrative learning pathway reduced to review-and-certify.

source_task_text: Inventory and track organizational equipment and capital assets
rationale: ◉ CLD (Low). Asset management software with AI tracking substantially compresses inventory work. Limited developmental depth as a learning mechanism; hence low severity.

source_task_text: Develop and manage equipment maintenance schedules and protocols
rationale: AI maintenance scheduling assists; judgment about which assets are critical-path for field operations requires organizational and ecological knowledge.

source_task_text: Plan capital replacement cycles and make equipment acquisition decisions
rationale: AI capital modeling assists; acquisition decisions require integrated knowledge of program needs and budget constraints. T3 planning → H2.

source_task_text: Manage facility maintenance schedules and service contracts
rationale: CMMS platforms substantially compress maintenance scheduling and work order management. C-position Ac: low severity — administrative overhead reduction with minimal career consequence.

source_task_text: Oversee facility operations to support program delivery
rationale: Operational judgment about facility conditions and vendor coordination requires organizational knowledge. AI assists tracking but not operational judgment.

source_task_text: Plan facility upgrades and capital improvements to meet organizational needs
rationale: Planning requires integration of organizational needs, budget, and building systems knowledge. T3 planning → H2.

source_task_text: Identify procurement needs and develop purchasing specifications
rationale: AI specification tools assist; which specifications are non-negotiable for environmental work quality requires program knowledge.

source_task_text: Execute procurement processes and vendor selection
rationale: Digital procurement platforms (SAM.gov, e-procurement systems) compress vendor search, bid solicitation, and comparative evaluation. Human role: final vendor judgment and authorization. C-position Ac: low severity.

source_task_text: Manage vendor relationships and contract compliance
rationale: Vendor relationship management requires organizational knowledge and relational judgment about when to escalate performance issues. AI tracking assists; relationship judgment is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Design and implement organizational records management systems
rationale: Records system design requires knowledge of organizational workflows, regulatory requirements, and information governance. System design judgment is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Maintain and organize organizational documentation and compliance records
rationale: ◉ CLD (Moderate). Digital records platforms with AI-assisted filing and compliance tracking substantially compress records maintenance. Entry-level practitioners have historically learned organizational accountability structures through records work; compression reduces this function.

source_task_text: Ensure records compliance with regulatory and funder requirements
rationale: AI compliance checking assists; which records meet substantive requirements for this specific regulatory context requires professional judgment.

source_task_text: Design and implement organizational digital financial management infrastructure
rationale: DC Primary. System architecture decisions are practitioner-primary; AI assists configuration but not design judgment.

source_task_text: Configure data-driven budgeting models and real-time financial dashboards
rationale: DC Primary. Dashboard configuration requires technical knowledge of financial data structures and organizational budget logic. Practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Monitor organizational financial position through automated reporting systems
rationale: ⚠️ Mode-Split. At organizations with mature automated financial platforms (Sage Intacct, Adaptive Insights), the system continuously generates financial position reports and dashboards. Practitioner supervises outputs and interprets anomalies. Automated system is primary monitoring actor → V at modal deployment. Smaller organizations without automation → A. ⚑ Delphi: mode-split scope.

source_task_text: Identify and evaluate conservation finance instruments applicable to organizational programs
rationale: SC Primary. AI literature tools assist; evaluating instrument appropriateness for this organization's legal capacity, funder relationships, and risk tolerance requires integrated professional judgment. T1 → H2.

source_task_text: Structure and negotiate conservation finance agreements with investors and regulators
rationale: H: criterion (a) and (b). Conservation finance structuring involves the practitioner's credibility with investors and legal authority to commit the organization. X-position: specialist territory requiring established investor/regulatory relationships. ⚑ Delphi: X vs. C boundary.

source_task_text: Monitor and report on conservation finance instrument performance
rationale: AI monitoring assists; reporting on conservation outcomes to investors requires professional judgment about ecological performance meaning. T3 monitoring → H1.

source_task_text: Develop organizational strategy for digital payment and cryptocurrency acceptance
rationale: DC Primary. Strategy requires technical knowledge of regulatory landscape and organizational risk tolerance. T1 planning → H2.

source_task_text: Configure and manage digital payment systems and cryptocurrency wallets
rationale: DC Primary. Technical configuration and management requires practitioner-primary knowledge of custody protocols and compliance requirements.

source_task_text: Monitor and report on digital financial instrument performance and compliance
rationale: Blockchain analytics and automated compliance reporting compress monitoring. Human role: review, interpret anomalies, certify. C-position Ac: low severity.

source_task_text: Design and implement automated financial workflows and compliance monitoring systems
rationale: DC Primary. System architecture requires technical knowledge of financial automation platforms and compliance logic. Practitioner-primary in design.

source_task_text: Supervise automated financial processing and AI compliance outputs
rationale: DC Primary. Deployed AI compliance systems perform continuous financial processing and generate compliance reports. Practitioner supervises outputs, validates exception handling, authorizes exceptions. Automated system is primary executor → V. ⚑ Delphi: validate whether practitioner role at modal deployment is genuinely supervisory.

source_task_text: Validate and correct AI-generated financial and compliance outputs
rationale: Validation requires professional judgment about which AI outputs are substantively correct vs. technically complete but wrong. Review function retains meaningful practitioner content — A not Ac.

source_task_text: Design real-time impact measurement systems linking financial and ecological outcomes
rationale: DC Primary. System design requires integrated knowledge of ecological monitoring, financial accounting, and reporting standards. T1 planning → H2.

source_task_text: Operate and maintain real-time impact dashboards and reporting platforms
rationale: DC Primary. At organizations with deployed real-time impact platforms, automated system continuously aggregates ecological and financial data and generates transparency reports. Practitioner supervises and validates data quality. V at modal deployment. Parallel to 3.4.1 T3 and 3.4.4 T2. ⚑ Delphi.

source_task_text: Synthesize impact measurement findings for investor and stakeholder reporting
rationale: Synthesis of measurement data into accountability narratives requires integrated judgment about organizational credibility. AI assists drafting; professional synthesis is primary. T3 synthesis → H2.

source_task_text: Assess organizational technology needs and develop digital transformation strategy
rationale: AI landscape scanning assists; judgment about what digital transformation means for this organization's mission and culture requires integrated leadership knowledge. T1 → H2.

source_task_text: Lead organizational change management for technology adoption
rationale: H: criterion (a) and (c). Change management requires the presence of a trusted leader whose relational authority enables genuine adoption. Real-time reading of staff resistance and uncertainty cannot be mediated through AI without losing the change quality. The practitioner's credibility with the organization is the professional contribution.

source_task_text: Evaluate and adapt digital transformation progress against organizational goals
rationale: Adaptive evaluation requires multi-dimensional assessment of human and technical factors. T3 monitoring/evaluation → H1.

source_task_text: Design distributed team structures, communication norms, and accountability systems
rationale: System design requires organizational knowledge of what accountability structures work for this team's roles and culture. T1 planning → H2.

source_task_text: Lead distributed teams through regular coordination and culture maintenance
rationale: H: criterion (a) and (c). Distributed team leadership requires the practitioner's ongoing relational presence — the trusted relationship that makes remote accountability feel supportive rather than surveilled and sustains organizational culture across distance.

source_task_text: Identify and address distributed team performance and culture challenges
rationale: H: criterion (a). Addressing performance and culture challenges in distributed teams requires the practitioner's relationship with specific team members — the relational trust that makes difficult conversations productive. AI cannot conduct the conversation that matters without losing the relationship that enables it.

source_task_text: Assess organizational stress indicators and design resilience-building interventions
rationale: AI assists in aggregating survey and attrition data; judgment about what patterns mean for this organization's resilience is practitioner-primary. T1 → H2.

source_task_text: Lead organizational culture development and change management
rationale: H: criterion (a). Organizational culture development requires the practitioner's sustained relational presence and institutional credibility over time — culture is built through consistent leadership behavior that staff observe and internalize.

source_task_text: Coach and support staff and managers through organizational change
rationale: H: criterion (a). Coaching requires the sustained relational trust between coach and coachee that makes it possible to hear difficult feedback and act on it. ⚑ Delphi: AI coaching tools advancing rapidly — validate H defensibility at 5-year horizon.

source_task_text: Assess generational and technological diversity needs within the organization
rationale: AI diagnostic tools assist; judgment about what diversity patterns mean for organizational effectiveness is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Design and facilitate cross-generational knowledge exchange and collaboration
rationale: H: criterion (c). Facilitating cross-generational exchange requires real-time reading of interpersonal dynamics between practitioners with different professional socialization and technological comfort. The facilitation creates knowledge transfer conditions that would not occur otherwise.

source_task_text: Evaluate cross-generational collaboration outcomes and adapt approaches
rationale: Adaptive evaluation requires multi-dimensional assessment of knowledge transfer and cultural inclusion. T3 → H2.

source_task_text: Develop organizational AI ethics governance frameworks and policies
rationale: AI ethics framework development requires integrated knowledge of AI capabilities, organizational risk tolerance, and governance design. T1 planning → H2.

source_task_text: Evaluate AI system deployments against ethics frameworks and organizational values
rationale: Evaluation requires judgment about whether AI system behavior meets the spirit of governance commitments — multi-dimensional assessment integrating technical understanding with institutional accountability.

source_task_text: Lead organizational accountability processes when AI systems produce problematic outcomes
rationale: H: criterion (b). Organizational accountability when AI systems fail requires a leader with institutional authority to own the failure, commit to remediation, and navigate accountability with affected stakeholders. Who is in the room determines whether accountability is genuine. X-position: senior leadership territory.

source_task_text: Conduct materiality assessment to identify ESG priorities for organizational strategy
rationale: AI materiality scanning tools assist; judgment about which issues are material for this organization's sector and stakeholder relationships is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Develop integrated ESG strategy aligned with business model and stakeholder commitments
rationale: Strategy requires integrated knowledge of regulatory landscape, investor expectations, and operational feasibility. T2 planning → H2.

source_task_text: Manage ESG strategy implementation across organizational functions
rationale: Implementation management requires sustained judgment about whether activities produce genuine ESG performance vs. compliance theater — ecological and institutional knowledge that AI cannot reliably apply.

source_task_text: Collect and validate ESG performance data for sustainability reporting
rationale: ◉ CLD (High). AI GHG accounting platforms (Watershed, Persefoni, Greenly) and Scope 1/2/3 automated calculators substantially compress emissions data collection and validation. Entry-level ESG analysts have historically developed sustainability literacy through manual data collection — compression eliminates the primary mechanism through which measurement connects to organizational reality. Highest-severity non-3.1 CLD signal in Domain 3.

source_task_text: Draft sustainability reports compliant with GRI, TCFD, or SEC climate disclosure requirements
rationale: AI reporting tools (CDP automation, GRI digital taxonomy) compress disclosure drafting by auto-populating standard sections and generating disclosure language from data inputs. Human role: substantive review, narrative judgment, and governance sign-off. C-position Ac: moderate-high severity — report drafting has been primary mechanism for developing sustainability governance literacy.

source_task_text: Manage sustainability disclosure governance and stakeholder communication
rationale: H: criterion (b). Disclosure governance is an institutional accountability act — who manages it and under what authority determines whether it is received as credible by investors and regulators.

source_task_text: Map and prioritize sustainability stakeholders and design engagement strategy
rationale: AI stakeholder mapping assists; judgment about which stakeholders are most consequential for this organization's sustainability credibility requires sector and institutional history knowledge.

source_task_text: Lead investor, community, and regulatory engagement on sustainability performance
rationale: H: criterion (a) and (b). Investor and regulatory engagement requires the practitioner's established credibility and institutional authority — the accountability relationship between who engages and what commitments are made determines whether engagement is substantive.

source_task_text: Evaluate stakeholder engagement outcomes and adapt sustainability communication
rationale: Adaptive evaluation requires judgment about whether engagement is building trust and credibility that enables genuine accountability. T3 → H2.

source_task_text: Design and execute stakeholder surveys and input processes for materiality assessment
rationale: AI survey tools assist; designing engagement processes that produce substantive input requires methodological and relational judgment.

source_task_text: Analyze and synthesize stakeholder input to develop organizational materiality matrix
rationale: AI materiality analysis platforms compress stakeholder input aggregation and priority mapping. Human role: review whether materiality assessment reflects genuine organizational risk rather than benchmark-averaging. C-position Ac: moderate severity.

source_task_text: Secure board and leadership endorsement of materiality framework
rationale: H: criterion (b). Board endorsement is a governance accountability event — who presents the framework under what institutional authority determines whether it produces genuine board commitment. X-position: senior leadership territory. ⚑ Delphi: X vs. C boundary.

source_task_text: Design sustainability metrics framework with indicators, baselines, and data protocols
rationale: DC Primary. Metrics framework design requires integrated knowledge of ecological measurement, organizational data capacity, and ESG reporting standards. T1 planning → H2.

source_task_text: Operate and manage sustainability data collection and KPI reporting systems
rationale: DC Primary. At organizations with deployed ESG data platforms (Sustainability Cloud, EcoVadis), automated system continuously aggregates performance data and generates reporting outputs. Practitioner supervises, validates data quality, interprets anomalies. V at modal deployment. Parallel to 3.4.1 T3 and 3.4.4 T2.

source_task_text: Synthesize sustainability performance findings and communicate to leadership and stakeholders
rationale: Synthesis translating KPI data into organizational accountability narrative requires integrated judgment distinguishing genuine progress from metric-gaming and contextualizing results against sector benchmarks. T3 synthesis → H2.

source_task_text: Assess current material flows and identify circular economy transition opportunities
rationale: AI material flow tools assist; identifying which circular opportunities are strategically viable for this organization's supplier and customer relationships requires integrated judgment.

source_task_text: Design circular business models and implementation roadmaps
rationale: SC Primary. Strategy design requires integrated knowledge of business model innovation, supply chain realities, and regulatory environment. T2 planning → H2.

source_task_text: Build partnerships and supply chain relationships to enable circular flows
rationale: H: criterion (a). Circular economy implementation depends on supplier and partner relationships — the trusted relationships enabling material take-back agreements and closed-loop supply partnerships. The practitioner's relational network and institutional credibility are the professional contribution.

source_task_text: Design waste reduction and zero waste program protocols and targets
rationale: Program design requires knowledge of operational waste generation patterns and sector benchmarks. T1 planning → H2.

source_task_text: Implement and manage waste reduction operations and diversion systems
rationale: Implementation management requires operational judgment about diversion performance and real-time adjustment. AI monitoring assists; operational judgment is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Monitor waste diversion performance and report on zero waste program outcomes
rationale: ◉ CLD (Moderate). Waste tracking software and automated reporting platforms compress waste data collection, diversion rate calculation, and reporting. Entry-level sustainability coordinators have historically developed waste management literacy through manual tracking.

source_task_text: Define LCA scope, system boundaries, and functional unit for product analysis
rationale: DC Primary. ⊗ Established-methodology rule (ISO 14040/14044). LCA scoping requires professional judgment about which system boundaries are scientifically defensible — scoping choices determine everything downstream. AI assists standard approach selection; scoping judgment is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Collect inventory data and execute LCA modeling using established methodology
rationale: DC Primary. ⊗ Established-methodology rule. LCA software platforms (SimaPro, OpenLCA) substantially compress computational execution — inventory compilation and impact characterization that previously took weeks now executes in hours. Human role: validate input assumptions, interpret results, certify outputs. C-position Ac: high severity — LCA computational execution was primary mechanism for developing environmental systems thinking. ⚑ Delphi: S boundary question for standardized product categories with mature ecoinvent databases. S-trajectory flag per Finding D3-3.

source_task_text: Interpret LCA results and translate into design recommendations and product strategy
rationale: DC Primary. Result interpretation requires integrated judgment about what hotspots mean for design feasibility and how to communicate findings to non-specialist decision-makers. T3 synthesis → H2.

source_task_text: Design reverse logistics and product take-back system architecture
rationale: SC Primary. System design requires integrated knowledge of logistics operations, supplier relationships, and regulatory requirements. T1 planning → H2.

source_task_text: Manage reverse logistics operations and closed-loop material flows
rationale: SC Primary. Operational management requires judgment about system degradation, contractor performance, and adaptive routing. AI tracking assists; operational judgment is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Track and optimize reverse logistics performance against circular economy targets
rationale: Logistics management platforms with AI optimization compress tracking and route efficiency analysis. Human role: review recommendations and authorize adjustments. C-position Ac: low severity.

source_task_text: Map organizational or supply chain material flows using MFA methodology
rationale: DC Primary. ⊗ Established-methodology rule. MFA system definition requires professional judgment about which material flows are analytically relevant — decisions determining analysis validity. AI assists data aggregation; methodological design is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Execute material flow quantification and identify waste generation points
rationale: DC Primary. ⊗ Established-methodology rule. MFA quantification platforms and digital supply chain tools substantially compress material flow tracking, loss point identification, and mass balance calculation. Human role: validate inputs, interpret anomalies, certify the material balance. C-position Ac: high severity — MFA execution was primary mechanism for developing material systems thinking. ⚑ Delphi: parallel S boundary question to 3.7.3 T2. S-trajectory flag per Finding D3-3.

source_task_text: Synthesize MFA results into circular economy optimization strategy
rationale: Synthesis translating material flow data into strategy requires integrated judgment about technical feasibility, economic viability, and organizational achievability. T3 synthesis → H2.

source_task_text: Establish vegetation monitoring plots; collect species composition, cover, density data
rationale: Drone cover estimation and AI-assisted plot photography deployed now; ground-truth plot establishment and botanical judgment remain human-executed. Augmentation, not Substitution.

source_task_text: Use digital data collection tools and GPS to record precise plot locations and measurements
rationale: GPS and mobile apps (Survey123, Fulcrum) are standard augmentation. Task is largely procedural tool operation; tacit density is low. ⚑ Delphi: has digital data tool adoption compressed plot data collection crew sizes (Ac threshold)?

source_task_text: Identify plant species in field using keys, apps, or expert consultation
rationale: AI plant ID apps (iNaturalist, PlantNet) deployed widely. Verification of difficult taxa, look-alike species, and condition-based ecological judgment remains human-led. Classified A because verification judgment is the primary professional contribution. ⚑ Delphi: are practitioners accepting AI identification without independent verification? If yes, reclassify toward V.

source_task_text: Conduct wildlife surveys using appropriate methods (transects, point counts, camera traps)
rationale: Camera trap AI ID (Wildlife Insights, MegaDetector) and acoustic monitoring with AI species classification deployed. Physical transect and point count execution remains human. Classified A on survey execution component.

source_task_text: Identify and interpret wildlife sign (tracks, scat, nests, feeding sign)
rationale: Sign interpretation requires embodied sensory engagement with landscape context. AI track recognition exists at low accuracy; behavioral interpretation of sign is not meaningfully automatable. Paradigm Human-Essential case. Among the strongest tacit knowledge claims in Domain 4.

source_task_text: Use digital tools to document observations and manage wildlife data
rationale: App-based documentation (eBird, iNaturalist, Survey123) is standard augmentation. Procedural tool use; low tacit content.

source_task_text: Collect water samples and conduct field measurements (temperature, pH, DO, turbidity)
rationale: Calibrated probes/meters augment measurement; collection and QC judgment remain human. Med tacit: protocols standardized but anomalous reading recognition is field-developed.

source_task_text: Conduct aquatic biological surveys (macroinvertebrates, fish, algae)
rationale: eDNA sampling maturing and partially displacing physical macroinvertebrate surveys for presence/absence detection. Physical sorting, electrofishing, and algae ID remain human-executed. Time Horizon 2 because eDNA is at deployment threshold. ⚑ Delphi: how far has eDNA penetrated as primary method in practitioners' organizations?

source_task_text: Use water quality sensors and data logging equipment
rationale: ⚠️ Mode-Split: deployed continuous monitoring sensor networks (sondes, data loggers) — the sensor is the primary data collector and the practitioner supervises. V is correct for deployed network mode. For single-measurement probe use in the field, A would apply. Classification reflects deployed network as the modal professional application at intermediate/advanced levels. Flag for Delphi adjudication of mode boundary.

source_task_text: Describe soil profiles and horizons using standard terminology and methods
rationale: Paradigm Human-Essential case. Soil profile description requires standing in a pit, Munsell color under field light, structure and consistence assessment by hand, horizon sequence integration with drainage indicators. No current technology meaningfully automates this interpretive process.

source_task_text: Collect soil samples for laboratory analysis (texture, nutrients, carbon, contaminants)
rationale: GPS-documented collection with app-based location and sample management. Physical collection is human-executed. ▶ Ro-Pending: automated soil coring systems exist in precision agriculture — not mainstream in environmental field operations. Flag for practitioner validation.

source_task_text: Conduct field tests of soil properties (texture by feel, infiltration, compaction)
rationale: Strongest tacit knowledge case in 4.1. Texture by feel — rolling soil to estimate clay content from plasticity and grittiness — is a paradigm embodied skill that cannot be reproduced by any current technology. Human-Essential.

source_task_text: Use mobile data collection apps to record field observations in real-time
rationale: Apps (Survey123, Fulcrum, ODK) are deployed standard tools. Task is procedural tool operation; tacit content belongs to the observations being recorded, not the app use.

source_task_text: Ensure data quality through validation, GPS accuracy checks, and photo documentation
rationale: Automated validation flags obvious errors; QC judgment — plausibility, adequacy, accuracy of GPS for monitoring purpose — remains human. Reclassified from C to P (session record): foundational data quality judgment is a P-level learning task even when performed imperfectly.

source_task_text: Sync field data with office databases and GIS systems
rationale: ◉ Career Ladder Destruction — Ac/P. Cloud sync and automated data pipeline tools have substantially compressed what was formerly manual data transfer and office-side entry work. Human role is workflow management and troubleshooting, not execution of transfer. Headcount compression in data management support roles plausible.

source_task_text: Implement restoration treatments including native planting, invasive removal, and soil amendments
rationale: Planting layout apps, GPS-guided site marking, and species selection tools are deployed augmentation. Physical planting, grubbing, and amendment work remains human-executed. Tacit Hi: microsite condition reading (moisture pockets, aspect variation, planting depth) determines success.

source_task_text: Operate restoration equipment (seed drills, tree planters, mulch blowers)
rationale: GPS-guided auto-steer seed drills exist and are used in large-scale restoration seeding. ▶ Ro-Pending: In current conservation/restoration contexts, GPS-guided mechanized planters are not yet the modal deployment; practitioner operates equipment with GPS augmentation. Classified A now; reclassify to Cv if auto-steer adoption in restoration contexts has crossed supervision threshold. ⚑ Delphi: what is the actual adoption rate of GPS-guided planting equipment in practitioners' restoration work contexts?

source_task_text: Monitor restoration sites and adapt techniques based on success
rationale: Drone imagery, remote sensing change detection, and AI-assisted cover analysis deployed. Adaptation decisions — reading why a treatment succeeded or failed — require tacit ecological judgment. C: monitoring and adaptive judgment emerge at intermediate proficiency; entry-level staff follow protocols.

source_task_text: Implement invasive species control using mechanical, chemical, or biological methods
rationale: AI-assisted detection and drone-based invasive mapping deployed for prioritization and targeting. Physical removal has no meaningful robotics exposure in conservation contexts. Chemical application via GPS-precision sprayers exists in agricultural contexts, not modal in environmental restoration. Tacit Hi: phenological timing and reinvasion risk judgment is field-developed.

source_task_text: Use integrated pest management approaches minimizing environmental impacts
rationale: IPM decision support tools deployed augmentation. Integration judgment — tools, combination, timing — is where professional value lies. C: IPM strategy design requires intermediate ecology; entry-level practitioners follow prescribed methods.

source_task_text: Monitor treatment effectiveness and adapt strategies
rationale: Drone monitoring, photo point analysis, AI vegetation change detection deployed. Trend interpretation and strategy adaptation require ecological judgment. C parallel to 4.2.1 T3.

source_task_text: Assist with prescribed fire operations following burn plans
rationale: Paradigm Human-Essential case for 4.2. No technology automates prescribed fire crew work — fireline maintenance, drip torch use, real-time fire behavior reading, situational awareness, escape route assessment. Among the highest tacit density in Domain 4. Primary site of foundational fire judgment development.

source_task_text: Monitor fire behavior and smoke during burns
rationale: Fire weather data feeds (RAWS, spot forecasts), real-time perimeter mapping, smoke dispersion models deployed augmentation. Monitoring judgment integrates model outputs with direct sensory observation of current fire behavior. C: behavior analysis judgment is intermediate-level; entry-level practitioners observe and report.

source_task_text: Maintain fire equipment and ensure crew safety
rationale: Crew safety oversight — reading crew fatigue, recognizing behavioral safety signals, real-time escape route verification — is Human-Essential and cannot be delegated to technology. P: foundational safety awareness is the first professional capacity developed in fire practitioners.

source_task_text: Install erosion control structures (check dams, wattles, silt fences)
rationale: Physical erosion control structure installation has no AI or robotics penetration in environmental field operations. Med tacit: site-specific placement decisions (where drainage concentration points occur, slope angle requiring closer spacing) add field judgment. P: installation is entry-level core work.

source_task_text: Implement bioengineering techniques for streambank stabilization
rationale: Highest tacit density in 4.2.4. Bioengineering (fascines, brush layers, live stakes, rootwads) requires reading bank hydrology, plant establishment dynamics, and integration of structural and biological mechanisms for site-specific conditions. No robotics or AI exposure. C: bioengineering judgment is intermediate-proficiency.

source_task_text: Monitor erosion control effectiveness and adapt treatments
rationale: Drone surveys and AI-assisted change detection (photogrammetric volume change, gully detection) deployed. Adaptation decisions remain human. C pattern parallel to 4.2.1 T3 and 4.2.2 T3.

source_task_text: Construct sustainable trail segments following design plans
rationale: Physical trail construction has no AI or robotics exposure in current environmental field operations. Med tacit: sustainable construction requires terrain reading (water concentration, substrate stability) beyond design specs. P: physical construction technique is foundational.

source_task_text: Maintain existing trails through brushing, drainage work, and tread repair
rationale: Physical trail maintenance has no meaningful automation at current deployment. Maintenance judgment — recognizing deteriorating drainage features before erosion compounds — is Med tacit. P: standard foundational crew work and primary site of technique learning.

source_task_text: Use appropriate tools and techniques for different trail types and conditions
rationale: Tool and technique selection for varied terrain and soil conditions — knowing when to excavate vs. fill, how to read substrate stability — is where trail expertise concentrates. Hi tacit: selection judgment is tacit and site-specific. C: tool selection and technique adaptation are intermediate-level proficiency.

source_task_text: Construct and maintain fireline using hand tools or equipment
rationale: Paradigm Human-Essential. Fireline construction under dynamic fire conditions requires continuous situational awareness, real-time terrain and fire behavior reading, and crew coordination. Primary site of foundational firefighter tacit knowledge development.

source_task_text: Implement firing operations to remove fuel ahead of fire
rationale: Firing operations require reading fire behavior, wind, and terrain in real time to direct ignition safely. C: firing leadership is an intermediate qualification (FFT1, squad boss level) requiring fire behavior judgment beyond entry-level.

source_task_text: Mop up hot spots and ensure fire containment
rationale: Mop-up requires tactile and sensory reading of smoldering combustion — probing for heat below surface, ensuring containment under changing conditions. Experienced firefighters develop sensory read of heat, smoke, and fuel conditions. P: foundational skill that every firefighter develops regardless of qualification level.

source_task_text: Develop comprehensive burn plans including objectives, prescriptions, and contingencies
rationale: Fire behavior modeling software (BehavePlus, FOFEM, CONSUME) and smoke dispersion modeling deployed standard practice. Practitioner drives modeling and integrates with site knowledge. C: burn plan development is intermediate-level; entry-level practitioners assist with data collection.

source_task_text: Conduct prescribed burns as burn boss ensuring objectives are met safely
rationale: Strongest Human-Essential in 4.3. Burn boss execution requires real-time synthesis of fire behavior, weather, smoke, crew positioning, public safety, and contingency activation — irreducibly human judgment under life-safety and resource-risk conditions. X: burn boss is advanced qualification (RXB1); career ladder destruction risk is not present at this position.

source_task_text: Monitor fire effects and document burn outcomes
rationale: Drone aerial monitoring during and post-burn, AI-assisted vegetation analysis from burn imagery, digital documentation systems deployed. Monitoring judgment — reading whether fire effects meet objectives — remains human. Ac considered and rejected: documentation automation has not compressed crew positions in prescribed fire monitoring.

source_task_text: Assess fuels and develop treatment strategies (mechanical thinning, prescribed fire, grazing)
rationale: LiDAR-derived canopy fuel data, FlamMap/FARSITE treatment effect modeling, AI-assisted fuel type classification from remote sensing deployed. Strategy development requires integrating ecological, operational, and fire behavior knowledge. C: fuels assessment and strategy development are intermediate-level proficiency.

source_task_text: Implement fuels treatments using appropriate methods and equipment
rationale: Physical fuels treatment execution — hand thinning, pruning, chipping, mowing, pile burning — has no meaningful robotics or AI exposure in conservation/public lands contexts at current deployment. Mechanized equipment is operator-controlled. P: physical treatment implementation is core foundational work.

source_task_text: Monitor treatment effectiveness using fuel models and fire behavior analysis
rationale: Post-treatment fuel models, FlamMap re-runs, remote sensing change detection deployed. Effectiveness interpretation and adaptive strategy revision are human. C: fuel model interpretation is intermediate-level.

source_task_text: Monitor fire weather and calculate fire danger indices
rationale: RAWS automated stations, fire danger calculators, fire weather platforms deployed standard tools. Human monitors, interprets, and acts on outputs. Med tacit: recognizing anomalous patterns and when indices diverge from observed conditions requires field judgment. P: weather monitoring is foundational for all fire practitioners during assignments.

source_task_text: Predict fire behavior using weather, fuels, and topography data
rationale: BehavePlus, FARSITE, FSPro, FlamMap deployed standard modeling tools. Professional value is in interpreting outputs against field conditions and recognizing when model assumptions fail — Hi tacit and human-irreducible. C: fire behavior prediction is intermediate-advanced proficiency (S-290, S-390 level).

source_task_text: Brief fire personnel on expected fire behavior and weather trends
rationale: Briefings synthesize technical analysis with operational accountability — communicating what matters to whom under time pressure, with life-safety consequence. Hi tacit: reading what a crew needs vs. what is technically available, making synthesis credible in field conditions. C: briefing requires intermediate-level behavior analysis competence and authority.

source_task_text: Assess post-fire conditions and erosion risk using BAER protocols
rationale: Satellite-derived burn severity mapping (dNBR), soil burn severity algorithms, ERMiT/WEPP erosion modeling deployed standard BAER tools. Ground-truthing of satellite data — verifying high-severity polygons against field conditions — is where Hi tacit concentrates. C: BAER assessment is intermediate-level proficiency.

source_task_text: Implement emergency stabilization treatments (mulching, seeding, barriers)
rationale: Physical post-fire erosion control installation has no meaningful automation. Med tacit: urgency and timing judgment (window between containment and first rainfall) adds non-protocol knowledge. P: foundational implementation work with time-critical learning value.

source_task_text: Monitor post-fire recovery and adapt restoration approaches
rationale: Repeat drone surveys, satellite time-series analysis, AI-assisted vegetation recovery detection deployed. Adaptive interpretation — distinguishing expected recovery from concerning patterns — is human judgment. C: recovery monitoring requires intermediate post-fire succession ecology.

source_task_text: Conduct job hazard analyses before field activities
rationale: Digital JHA templates and hazard checklist apps deployed; AI drafting of JHA documents from task descriptions is emerging. Defining contribution — recognizing non-obvious hazards in specific field conditions — is Hi tacit. C: leading JHAs requires intermediate-level risk recognition. ⚑ Delphi: if AI-assisted JHA generation compresses the cognitive work of hazard analysis, are early-career practitioners losing the developmental exercise of reasoning through risk independently?

source_task_text: Ensure crew members use appropriate PPE and follow safety protocols
rationale: Behavioral safety management — reading crew fatigue, compliance gap under time pressure, injury-risk behavior — is Human-Essential. Relational and observational judgment not substitutable by technology. C: crew safety oversight requires supervisory authority and relationship knowledge at intermediate proficiency.

source_task_text: Investigate incidents and near-misses to prevent recurrence
rationale: ◉ Career Ladder Ac/C. AI-assisted incident investigation report generation and root cause analysis frameworks increasingly producing first drafts. Investigation judgment — interviewing witnesses, reading physical scene, identifying systemic causes — remains human. Ac because documentation compression is real while investigation judgment is H. ⚑ Delphi: has AI-assisted incident documentation reduced the cognitive practice of constructing causal narratives in developing practitioners?

source_task_text: Assess injuries and provide first aid in remote locations
rationale: Field trauma assessment and treatment in remote settings — reading injury severity without diagnostics, improvising treatment with available resources, evacuation decision-making — is Human-Essential. Hi tacit: wilderness medicine judgment develops through scenario training and field experience. P: basic first aid is a foundational competency expectation for all field practitioners.

source_task_text: Coordinate medical evacuations when necessary
rationale: Satellite communication tools, GPS coordinate sharing, digital evacuation planning tools deployed. Evacuation coordination judgment — patient stability, terrain and weather constraints, timing tradeoffs — remains Human-Essential. AI vector at Time Horizon 2: AI-assisted evacuation routing and helicopter coordination tools in development for wilderness contexts. C: evacuation coordination requires intermediate-level wilderness medicine authority.

source_task_text: Maintain first aid supplies and medical certifications
rationale: ◉ Career Ladder Destruction — Ac/P. Inventory management systems, certification tracking apps, and automated restocking alerts substantially compress manual inventory and certification calendar management. Administrative compression; low developmental consequence (physical maintenance skill is not compressed).

source_task_text: Participate in search operations using established search patterns
rationale: AI-assisted probability of area modeling (SARTopo, CalTopo with AI lost-person behavior prediction) and drone-assisted aerial search deployed. Physical search — navigating terrain, recognizing clues, pattern discipline under fatigue — remains human. P: foundational search participation is entry-level.

source_task_text: Navigate to remote locations using map, compass, and GPS
rationale: GPS and digital navigation tools (CalTopo, OnX, Gaia) deployed standard augmentation alongside traditional navigation. Med tacit: route selection and terrain hazard judgment requires field experience. P: navigation is foundational for all field practitioners. ⚑ Delphi: has GPS augmentation begun to displace traditional navigation competence in early-career practitioners — creating a vulnerability in GPS-failure scenarios?

source_task_text: Provide emergency care and assist with evacuation
rationale: Emergency care and physical evacuation assistance — assisting injured subject across terrain, real-time care decisions, group management under stress — is Human-Essential. Note: drone-based supply delivery to subjects before rescue team arrival is emerging but does not change task classification at current deployment.

source_task_text: Identify potential hazardous materials in field settings
rationale: AI-assisted hazmat identification tools, digital SDS databases, drone-based remote assessment of suspected hazmat sites deployed. Recognition of potential hazard from sensory field cues remains human. P: hazmat awareness is foundational safety expectation.

source_task_text: Implement appropriate containment and notification procedures
rationale: Containment and notification judgment — severity assessment, response sequencing, resource determination under uncertainty — is Human-Essential. C: hazmat response beyond awareness (HAZWOPER Operations level) is intermediate proficiency.

source_task_text: Use personal protective equipment for hazmat situations
rationale: PPE selection and use in active hazmat situations requires real-time contamination risk judgment, PPE limitation awareness, and donning/doffing under field conditions — tacit judgment that training creates and deployment tests. P: foundational safety competency.

source_task_text: Use radios, satellite phones, and emergency beacons to communicate during incidents
rationale: Communication technology (satellite messengers, digital radio systems, dispatch integration apps) deployed standard augmentation. Communication judgment — priority, clarity, crisis communication under stress — is human. P: foundational communication competency for all field practitioners.

source_task_text: Document incidents thoroughly following organizational protocols
rationale: ◉ Career Ladder Ac/C. AI-assisted incident report drafting and standardized digital documentation platforms substantially compress incident documentation time. Lo tacit: reporting format is procedural; investigative judgment is in 4.4.1 T3. ⚑ Delphi: does AI compression of incident report writing reduce the cognitive practice of constructing narrative accounts, impairing analytical thinking development in contributing-level practitioners?

source_task_text: Coordinate with emergency responders and dispatch centers
rationale: Multi-agency emergency coordination — managing information flows between field teams, dispatch, medical resources, and command — is Human-Essential. Hi tacit: experienced coordinators develop read of organizational dynamics, resource availability, and communication load management under active emergency. C: coordination requires intermediate ICS competence and institutional relationships.

source_task_text: Select and use appropriate hand tools for vegetation management, trail work, and restoration
rationale: Hand tool selection and use has no AI or robotics exposure at current deployment. Physical technique and selection judgment are purely tacit, developed through practice. P: most basic entry-level physical proficiency in Domain 4.

source_task_text: Maintain tools in safe working condition through sharpening and repair
rationale: Tool maintenance is embodied physical skill — reading edge quality, identifying handle stress, knowing repair limits — with no meaningful automation. P: foundational equipment responsibility for all field staff.

source_task_text: Transport and store tools safely
rationale: Procedural task with minimal tacit content. H because no technology automates this physical responsibility. Lo tacit: protocols are well-specified. P: foundational safety behavior. Lowest analytical significance task in Domain 4 — present for taxonomy completeness.

source_task_text: Operate chainsaws safely for tree falling, bucking, and limbing
rationale: Chainsaw operation — felling decisions, hinge wood control, kickback avoidance, tree lean and stress reading — is among the most tacit and safety-critical physical skills in Domain 4. No automation exists for in-field chainsaw judgment. P: foundational chainsaw competency built through supervised practice.

source_task_text: Use string trimmers, brush cutters, and mowers for vegetation management
rationale: Power equipment for vegetation management is physical skill with no meaningful automation in varied terrain and vegetation conditions of environmental field operations. Robotic mowers exist in commercial grounds maintenance but not in environmental field operations contexts. P: standard foundational field competency.

source_task_text: Maintain and troubleshoot small engines
rationale: Digital diagnostic tools, AI-assisted troubleshooting guides, manufacturer diagnostic software deployed augmentation. Hi tacit component in field diagnosis — reading vibration, smell, sound with limited tools — retained. C: engine troubleshooting emerges at intermediate proficiency; entry-level performs basic maintenance.

source_task_text: Operate tractors, excavators, or skid steers for restoration or construction
rationale: ▶ Ro-Pending. GPS-guided auto-steer deployed at scale in agricultural contexts (Time Horizon 1 there). In environmental restoration and construction contexts — modal use case for this competency — GPS-guided auto-steer and semi-autonomous excavator/skid steer operation at Time Horizon 2 (3–5 years). Physical operation for ecological grading, channel reconstruction, and restoration earthwork requires continuous terrain-reading judgment that is Hi tacit. A rather than V at current deployment reality. Not Cv: AI image analysis is not simultaneously active with robotic guidance on this operational task at current deployment. ⚑ Delphi: what is the actual adoption rate of GPS-guided auto-steer in restoration-context heavy equipment?

source_task_text: Drive four-wheel drive vehicles in off-road conditions
rationale: Off-road vehicle operation — reading surface stability, selecting lines, managing traction on slopes — is Hi tacit judgment developed through field experience. No meaningful automation at current deployment for off-road environmental field vehicles. P: basic vehicle operation is foundational for all field staff.

source_task_text: Perform pre-trip inspections and basic maintenance
rationale: ◉ Career Ladder Destruction — Ac/P. Digital pre-trip inspection checklists, telematics systems tracking vehicle condition, automated maintenance scheduling substantially compress manual inspection logging and fleet coordination. Physical inspection tasks remain; administrative coordination is Ac-compressed. Lo tacit: inspection procedure is protocol-driven.

source_task_text: Operate drones safely following FAA regulations for environmental monitoring
rationale: Cv — explicit boundary reasoning. FAA-regulated drone operation involves simultaneous AI and robotic exposure on the same task: (1) the UAS is a physical robotic system being operated, and (2) AI flight planning, obstacle avoidance, and automated modes are active simultaneously. Both vectors are inseparable during the same flight operation → Cv. Med tacit: FAA compliance and safe flight are protocol-governed, but weather windows, terrain hazards, and subject wildlife behavior during flight add field judgment. P: drone operation is increasingly foundational with Part 107 certification as a baseline expectation.

source_task_text: Capture aerial imagery and video for site assessment or mapping
rationale: ◉ PRIMARY CAREER LADDER DESTRUCTION SIGNAL — V/Cv/P. Modern drone platforms fly automated grid/orbit missions autonomously; the human supervises the automated flight, monitors for safety anomalies, and manages capture settings. The drone is the primary data collection actor during automated missions — V by current deployment reality. Cv: automated flight system (Ro) and AI flight planning/object avoidance (AI) are simultaneously active. P: image capture is an entry-level drone application and primary site of skill development — but automation supervision is not equivalent to learning experiential data collection judgment. Career ladder disruption mechanism: entry-level practitioners are placed in oversight roles over autonomous systems before developing the ecological and technical judgment needed to recognize when automated outputs are wrong.

source_task_text: Process drone data to create orthomosaics, 3D models, or vegetation maps
rationale: Photogrammetry software (Pix4D, Agisoft, DroneDeploy) automates primary processing pipeline; AI vegetation classification augments analysis. Practitioner configures parameters, QCs outputs, interprets results. C: data processing requires intermediate photogrammetry, GIS, and ecological interpretation. Note: T3 is Datacraft in character, crossing into Domain 2 territory — expected given hybrid nature of UAS competencies.

source_task_text: Perform scheduled maintenance on equipment and vehicles
rationale: ◉ Career Ladder Destruction — Ac/P. Digital maintenance scheduling systems, telematics alerts, AI-assisted maintenance interval prediction substantially compress manual tracking and scheduling. Physical maintenance tasks (oil changes, filter replacement, lubrication) remain human-executed; administrative coordination is Ac-compressed. Lo tacit: scheduled maintenance follows manufacturer protocols.

source_task_text: Diagnose equipment problems and make repairs
rationale: AI-assisted diagnostic tools, digital troubleshooting trees, manufacturer remote diagnostic systems deployed. Hi tacit in field diagnosis — reading vibration, smell, sound with limited tools, improvising repairs with available parts — irreducibly experiential. C: equipment diagnosis and repair emerges at intermediate proficiency.

source_task_text: Manage maintenance records and parts inventory
rationale: Fleet management software, parts inventory systems with automated reorder points, digital maintenance record platforms substantially compress manual record-keeping. Administrative coordination. Lo tacit: data entry and inventory management procedural. C: maintenance program management requires intermediate understanding of equipment lifecycles and procurement.

source_task_text: Implement cover cropping, diverse rotations, and reduced tillage systems
rationale: AI-assisted cover crop species selection tools, precision planting guidance, and tillage optimization software deployed augmentation. Ecological judgment — reading soil conditions, selecting species mixes, adapting timing to weather and cropping context — is Hi tacit and remains human-executed. P: cover cropping implementation is entry-level agricultural practice.

source_task_text: Integrate livestock using rotational grazing or other regenerative approaches
rationale: Livestock integration judgment — reading animal behavior, forage condition, water access, stress signals across paddock moves — is Hi tacit and Human-Essential at current deployment. AI grazing management apps and sensor-based paddock monitoring at Time Horizon 2. C: livestock integration requires intermediate agricultural ecology; entry-level practitioners follow prescribed rotation schedules.

source_task_text: Monitor and adapt regenerative farming systems based on ecological indicators
rationale: Digital monitoring platforms, AI-assisted soil health trend analysis, remote sensing vegetation indices deployed augmentation. Adaptive ecological judgment — why a system is or isn't performing and what to change — is Hi tacit. C: adaptive systems management requires intermediate agricultural ecology and systems thinking.

source_task_text: Operate GPS-guided tractors and implements for precise planting and application
rationale: ◉ PRIMARY CAREER LADDER DESTRUCTION SIGNAL — V/Cv/P. GPS-guided auto-steer tractors are deployed at scale in commercial agriculture. Auto-steer system executes precise field navigation autonomously; operator supervises, monitors for anomalies, manages headland turns. V by current deployment reality: automated system is primary task executor. Cv — explicit boundary reasoning: physical auto-steer guidance system (Ro) and AI prescription map management (AI) are operationally inseparable during the same planting pass → Cv. Med tacit: supervising automated operation requires field knowledge to recognize system failures, but substantially less tacit than non-automated equipment operation. P: equipment operation is entry-level in precision agriculture contexts. Career ladder disruption mechanism: entry-level practitioners develop automation supervision judgment rather than embodied equipment operation skills; the tacit substrate supporting intelligent supervision is not being formed.

source_task_text: Use soil sensors, yield monitors, and drone imagery for site-specific management
rationale: Cv classification. Soil sensors (AI-processed), yield monitors (GPS+sensor integration), and drone imagery (UAS + AI analysis) are used in combination for the same site-specific management decision. When used together as described, the same decision faces simultaneous AI and physical platform exposure → Cv. A rather than V: practitioner actively interprets and makes decisions from data streams rather than supervising an automated system. C: integrating multiple precision data streams requires intermediate understanding of soil-crop relationships and technology integration.

source_task_text: Develop and implement variable rate application prescriptions
rationale: AI-assisted prescription generation software (using soil test data, yield maps, satellite imagery) produces variable rate maps for practitioner review and implementation. Practitioner contribution: agronomic plausibility judgment, site-knowledge adjustment, implementation oversight. ⚑ Delphi: in contexts where AI prescription generation is highly automated, has this crossed the Ac threshold — with agronomist time investment significantly compressed to review-and-certify?

source_task_text: Scout crops for pests and monitor population levels against action thresholds
rationale: AI-assisted pest identification apps, automated trap monitoring, drone-based crop scouting deployed augmentation. Physical scouting — walking fields, reading plant symptoms, finding early instar stages that automated systems miss — retains Hi tacit content. P: crop scouting is entry-level agricultural practice and primary site of pest identification skill development.

source_task_text: Implement cultural, biological, and chemical pest control as part of IPM programs
rationale: IPM decision support tools guide treatment selection; precision application equipment with GPS targeting deployed. Physical implementation requires timing and dosage judgment. C: IPM strategy implementation requires intermediate pest ecology and agricultural systems knowledge.

source_task_text: Document pest management activities and evaluate effectiveness
rationale: ◉ Career Ladder Ac/C. Digital record-keeping platforms, AI-assisted effectiveness analysis, automated regulatory compliance documentation substantially compress IPM record-keeping and reporting. Lo tacit: documentation protocol-driven. Ac is cleaner here than in 4.4.1 T3 because effectiveness analysis itself is increasingly AI-assisted, compressing analytical time investment for mid-career IPM practitioners.

source_task_text: Schedule irrigation based on crop water needs, soil moisture, and weather
rationale: V classification. Weather-based automated irrigation controllers and AI-driven scheduling systems (ET models, soil moisture sensor networks, weather forecasts) deployed at scale in commercial agriculture and increasingly in conservation programs. Systems schedule and execute irrigation autonomously; practitioner oversees, reviews, and overrides when sensors or models fail. V by current deployment reality. C: irrigation system oversight requires intermediate understanding of crop water relationships; entry-level practitioners operate systems following established schedules.

source_task_text: Operate and maintain irrigation systems (drip, sprinkler, flood)
rationale: Automated systems control valves and timing; physical operation — leak checking, pressure testing, drip system clog management, sprinkler adjustment — remains human-executed. Med tacit: reading system performance from physical indicators. P: irrigation system operation is foundational agricultural practice.

source_task_text: Implement water conservation practices and technologies
rationale: Deficit irrigation scheduling tools, soil moisture-based automation, water use efficiency analytics deployed augmentation. Conservation technology implementation requires agronomic judgment for site-specific configuration. C: conservation technology implementation requires intermediate water management knowledge.

source_task_text: Conduct soil health assessments using field tests and laboratory analysis
rationale: Soil health assessment apps, AI-assisted test result interpretation, digital field assessment tools deployed augmentation. Field tests — aggregate stability, infiltration, earthworm counts, slaking — require physical execution and site-reading judgment that is Hi tacit. P: soil health assessment is entry-level in agricultural conservation contexts.

source_task_text: Implement practices that build soil organic matter and biological activity
rationale: Soil health management implementation — cover crop termination timing, compost application rate and placement, reduced tillage adaptation to field conditions — requires ecological judgment about how current soil conditions should inform management choices. Irreducible Fieldcraft contribution: reading soil, crop, and weather interactions in real time. No meaningful automation at current deployment for adaptive implementation judgment. C: soil health management requires intermediate agricultural ecology.

source_task_text: Monitor soil health trends and adapt management
rationale: AI-assisted soil health trend analysis, satellite-derived vegetation indices as soil biological activity proxies, digital monitoring platforms deployed augmentation. Adaptive management judgment — interpreting why metrics are or aren't improving — is Hi tacit. C: trend interpretation and adaptive response require intermediate ecological systems knowledge.

source_task_text: Install bioswales, rain gardens, and permeable pavement for stormwater management
rationale: Confirms 4.2 pattern hypothesis. Physical installation — excavating bioswale cells, placing media layers, establishing grading, setting permeable pavement substrate — has no meaningful AI or robotics exposure at current deployment. Urban construction equipment is operator-controlled. Med tacit: reading existing drainage patterns, soil conditions, and design intent against site reality. P: installation assistance is foundational entry-level work.

source_task_text: Construct green roofs and living walls
rationale: Higher tacit density than bioswale installation: reading structural load capacity, sequencing waterproofing/drainage/media layers with integrity judgment, plant selection for constrained rooftop conditions. No robotics or AI exposure. C: green roof/living wall construction requires intermediate building systems, horticulture, and waterproofing knowledge — source text confirms intermediate as the level for full green roof installation.

source_task_text: Monitor green infrastructure performance and maintain installations
rationale: Digital performance monitoring platforms (sensor networks, flow meters, infiltration monitoring), AI-assisted performance trend analysis, drone-based visual inspection deployed augmentation. Physical maintenance remains human-executed. C: performance interpretation and adaptive maintenance require intermediate stormwater system function knowledge.

source_task_text: Plant and establish trees using appropriate techniques for urban conditions
rationale: Urban tree planting involves substantially higher tacit density than rural planting: reading soil compaction and drainage constraints, recognizing below-grade infrastructure conflicts not visible on plans, establishing aftercare appropriate to urban stress factors (heat island, drought, reflected radiation). Hi tacit: urban site-reading is qualitatively distinct from standard horticultural planting. P: planting is foundational entry-level work and primary site of urban site-reading skill development.

source_task_text: Prune trees following ISA standards for health, safety, and structure
rationale: Strongest tacit knowledge case in 4.7. ISA-standard pruning requires reading tree architecture — branch attachments, included bark, decay presence at junctions — making irreversible cuts affecting structure for decades. No technology automates this judgment. Ro-adjacency hypothesis test result: aerial lifts, chippers, and stump grinders are operator-controlled powered equipment, categorically equivalent to 4.5.2 power tools — not robotic systems. Hi tacit: structural pruning judgment develops through ISA training and mentored field experience. C: structural pruning requires ISA Certified Arborist-level knowledge.

source_task_text: Assess and manage urban tree health, pests, and diseases
rationale: Human-Essential at current deployment with AI augmentation trajectory — Time Horizon 2. ISA-standard tree health assessment requires probing decay with mallet, reading crown dieback patterns, identifying pest frass, integrating visual and tactile cues into diagnosis. Embodied sensory engagement is irreplaceable at current deployment → H. AI tree health diagnostic apps (drone crown assessment, AI symptom identification from photos) advancing toward deployment → AI vector at Time Horizon 2. C: diagnosis requires ISA Certified Arborist-level knowledge. ⚑ Delphi: at what proficiency threshold does AI-assisted diagnosis adequately substitute for in-person assessment?

source_task_text: Inspect and clean stormwater infrastructure (catch basins, pipes, outlets)
rationale: ▶ Ro-Pending. Robotic pipe inspection systems (CCTV crawlers, robotic catch basin inspectors) are commercially deployed in municipal stormwater contexts. Human-conducted physical inspection remains the dominant mode across most settings in this competency's scope. A reflects modal deployment; Time Horizon 2 for Ro because robotic inspection penetration is accelerating. ⚑ Delphi: in municipal MS4 programs specifically, has robotic pipe inspection displaced human inspection as the primary method? If yes, reclassify to V/Ro.

source_task_text: Monitor stormwater quality and implement pollution prevention
rationale: Real-time stormwater quality sensors, automated sampling systems, AI-assisted discharge analysis deployed augmentation. Illicit discharge investigation — tracing sources through a system, reading visual/olfactory cues, smoke/dye testing — requires field judgment that is Med tacit. C: stormwater quality monitoring and pollution prevention require intermediate MS4/NPDES regulatory knowledge.
