source_task_text: Review existing policies to assess alignment with conservation objectives
rationale: AI policy research tools assist; assessing alignment with conservation objectives requires professional legal and ecological judgment. Practitioner-primary throughout.

source_task_text: Compare federal, state, and local environmental laws affecting a project area
rationale: ◉ S — CONFIRMED STRESS TEST CALL. AI legal research and regulatory comparison tools (Westlaw AI, LexisNexis AI, LLM regulatory synthesis) execute multi-jurisdictional law comparison at deployment threshold. P-position CLD: regulatory reasoning development pathway eliminated.

source_task_text: Prepare memos or policy briefs summarizing legal considerations
rationale: ◉ CLD (Moderate). AI drafting tools (LLM memo generation, policy brief templates) substantially compress memo and brief production. Practitioner review-and-certify for accuracy, framing, and defensibility. P-position: professional writing development pathway partially compressed.

source_task_text: Conduct field inspections and desktop reviews to ensure activities meet legal requirements
rationale: Field inspection requires site-specific regulatory and ecological judgment; desktop review AI-assisted. Practitioner primary as combined inspection and compliance evaluator. Hi tacit for field component. C: compliance assessment requires intermediate regulatory knowledge.

source_task_text: Develop checklists and procedures for regulatory compliance
rationale: ◉ S — CONFIRMED STRESS TEST CALL. AI compliance checklist generators and procedure documentation tools deployed now for standard permit and regulatory compliance categories. Criterion 1 satisfied: practitioner's contribution reduces to reviewing AI-generated output. P-position CLD: compliance documentation development pathway eliminated.

source_task_text: Coordinate with regulatory agencies during audits or investigations
rationale: H: ARM (Accountability Relationship Mechanism). Coordination with regulatory agencies during formal proceedings requires institutional accountability and relational presence — who coordinates and under what professional authority determines how the agency interaction unfolds. AI cannot exercise this accountability relationship.

source_task_text: Guide staff or applicants through permit application processes
rationale: AI permit requirement lookup tools and digital permitting guides assist navigation; practitioner contribution is contextual interpretation — which pathway applies to this specific project, site, and regulatory history. Professional consultation requiring environmental law knowledge. A at C.

source_task_text: Review project proposals to determine permitting needs
rationale: Permitting needs determination requires legal and ecological judgment about which activities trigger which permitting thresholds in which jurisdictions. AI tools assist checklist review; practitioner primary on nexus and threshold determinations for non-standard projects. A at C.

source_task_text: Track permit status and coordinate timing with project implementation
rationale: Digital permit management and tracking systems (ePermitting platforms, agency portals, project management software with permit status integration) continuously monitor permit timelines and flag approaching deadlines. Practitioner supervises: reviews tracking outputs, escalates stalled permits, coordinates schedule adjustments. V at C. Lo tacit: monitoring is platform-managed.

source_task_text: Develop or review environmental assessments (EAs) or environmental impact statements (EISs)
rationale: EA/EIS development requires interdisciplinary synthesis: scoping analysis, alternatives development, impact characterization across all resource areas, mitigation measure design. AI assists document drafting and cross-reference checking. Practitioner primary throughout as lead author and legal quality controller. Hi tacit: interdisciplinary synthesis for complex projects. A at C.

source_task_text: Lead public scoping and comment periods in accordance with NEPA regulations
rationale: H: LSD (Live Social Dynamics Mechanism). Public scoping facilitation requires real-time reading of community interest, stakeholder dynamics, and public concern — determining which issues to elevate for detailed study, how to respond to challenging public engagement in the moment, and maintaining procedural legitimacy under public scrutiny. NEPA scoping is a legally defined public process where the practitioner's live facilitation judgment shapes the document's legal defensibility.

source_task_text: Coordinate interdisciplinary teams and documentation for NEPA compliance
rationale: H: ARM. NEPA interdisciplinary team coordination requires institutional accountability — the project lead who commits the agency to a NEPA timeline, manages resource specialist obligations, and authorizes document structure decisions is the legally responsible coordinator. AI project management tools assist scheduling; the accountability relationship that holds specialists to their analytical obligations is practitioner-primary.

source_task_text: Respond to reports of environmental violations on managed lands
rationale: Initial violation response and assessment requires regulatory judgment and site-specific knowledge — determining what is occurring, whether it constitutes a violation, what regulatory authority applies, and what response is appropriate. AI assists regulatory cross-referencing. Hi tacit: field assessment of violation conditions. A at C.

source_task_text: Document evidence and communicate findings to enforcement personnel
rationale: Evidence documentation and standardized violation reporting formats are substantially AI-assisted (digital field reporting apps, AI-assisted form completion, automated chain-of-custody documentation). Practitioner contribution: selecting which evidence to document, ensuring documentation meets legal evidentiary standards, and communicating findings with appropriate precision. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Support legal proceedings with accurate records and expert input
rationale: H: ARM. Expert testimony, deposition, and legal proceeding support requires professional credibility and accountability that are the non-substitutable element — the expert who prepared the analysis and can defend it under cross-examination. X: supporting legal proceedings is advanced-specialist function requiring deep regulatory and subject-matter expertise.

source_task_text: Develop multi-use plans that balance conservation, recreation, and development
rationale: Multi-use plan development requires synthesizing ecological, legal, social, and economic constraints into a defensible planning framework. AI scenario modeling tools assist; practitioner primary in value-laden trade-off decisions that give plans their policy substance. Hi tacit: place-specific knowledge of land conditions, use histories, and stakeholder dynamics. A at C.

source_task_text: Engage stakeholders to define land use goals and compatible uses
rationale: H: LSD. Stakeholder engagement for land use goal definition requires live reading of community interests, competing claims, and political dynamics — facilitating a process that builds durable consensus rather than recorded opposition. The practitioner's live presence, facilitation judgment, and relational credibility with diverse stakeholders are the non-substitutable contribution.

source_task_text: Synthesize biological, cultural, and economic data into planning documents
rationale: Data synthesis into planning documents requires professional integration of disparate analytical threads — connecting species inventory findings to zoning alternatives, economic analysis to mitigation measures, cultural resource sensitivities to access restrictions. AI assists data compilation and document drafting. A at C.

source_task_text: Apply zoning designations to reflect ecological sensitivity or legal mandates
rationale: Zoning designation requires legal and ecological judgment — matching site conditions and regulatory triggers to appropriate protection categories, handling boundary and transitional conditions. AI GIS tools assist analysis; practitioner primary on designation decisions. A at C.

source_task_text: Update land classifications based on new assessments or use trends
rationale: GIS-assisted classification update tools, automated remote sensing change detection, and database management systems substantially compress classification maintenance. Practitioner contribution: review automated updates for accuracy, adjudicate boundary cases, authorize classification changes with documentation. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Maintain geospatial data showing zoning boundaries and constraints
rationale: GIS database maintenance with automated update scripts, version control, and spatial integrity checking continuously maintains the spatial data record. Practitioner supervises: monitors data integrity reports, reviews automated updates, troubleshoots discrepancies. V at P: the oversight function is accessible to entry-level GIS practitioners. Lo tacit.

source_task_text: Coordinate interdisciplinary teams to draft forest, range, or refuge management plans
rationale: H: ARM. Interdisciplinary team coordination for management plan development requires institutional accountability — the project lead who commits the agency to plan content, manages specialist obligations under regulatory frameworks (NFMA, FLPMA), and maintains the team's procedural compliance is exercising institutional authority that AI cannot replicate.

source_task_text: Follow agency-specific planning frameworks and timelines
rationale: ◉ CLD (Low). Agency planning workflow management tools, automated timeline tracking, and template-based framework documentation compress the procedural compliance management of established planning processes. Practitioner contribution: review automated tracking, flag deviations, maintain documentation. Low developmental consequence: the learning value of management plan development concentrates in the synthesis and judgment functions of T1 and T3.

source_task_text: Incorporate climate, wildfire, and equity considerations into plan revisions
rationale: Integrating emerging science and policy directives (climate projections, wildfire risk modeling, EJ screening) into management plan revisions requires professional synthesis judgment about how best available science maps onto specific landscape conditions and management objectives. AI tools assist literature review and scenario projection. Hi tacit: place-specific knowledge. Horizon 2: climate integration methods are actively developing. A at C.

source_task_text: Align public land management plans with county or regional comprehensive plans
rationale: Cross-jurisdictional plan alignment requires knowledge of federal, state, and local planning frameworks and the legal relationships between them. AI tools assist cross-document analysis. Practitioner primary on alignment determinations and negotiation of inconsistencies. A at C.

source_task_text: Attend planning commission meetings to share agency priorities
rationale: H: ARM. Official participation in planning commission proceedings to represent agency positions requires institutional accountability — the agency representative's presence and statements constitute official agency positions in the formal record. AI cannot be sent to planning commission meetings as an agency representative.

source_task_text: Share geospatial data with local planners to support coordinated development
rationale: Data sharing via GIS portals, automated data publication systems, and standardized geospatial exchange formats substantially compress data coordination logistics. Practitioner contribution: ensuring data shared is current and appropriate for the coordination purpose, supporting local planners in interpreting shared data. Ac at P. Low developmental consequence.

source_task_text: Model future land use scenarios under varying ecological, social, or economic conditions
rationale: Land use scenario modeling requires professional judgment in scenario specification — what assumptions structure the ecological, social, and economic futures being explored, which scenarios are decision-relevant vs. purely theoretical. AI modeling platforms accelerate computation. Practitioner primary in scenario design. A at C.

source_task_text: Use participatory scenario planning workshops to explore trade-offs
rationale: H: LSD. Participatory scenario planning workshops require live facilitation of group deliberation about uncertain futures — guiding participants through productive disagreement about values and priorities without foreclosing legitimate conflict. The practitioner's real-time facilitation of trade-off exploration is the non-substitutable professional contribution.

source_task_text: Visualize scenario impacts with maps or decision-support tools
rationale: AI-assisted visualization production, automated map generation from scenario model outputs, and DSS dashboard tools substantially compress visualization execution. Practitioner contribution: design which visualizations serve the decision context, review for accuracy and audience-appropriateness. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Estimate the economic value of timber, water, recreation, or other resources using market and non-market methods
rationale: Resource valuation requires economic and ecological judgment: selecting appropriate valuation methods for each resource type and use context, handling non-market valuation challenges (existence value, passive use), and interpreting results against decision needs. AI tools assist computation. A at C.

source_task_text: Estimate economic value using market/non-market methods
rationale: Method selection judgment-intensive; AI assists but practitioner primary.

source_task_text: Conduct willingness-to-pay studies or contingent valuation surveys
rationale: Survey instrument design and contingent valuation methodology require economic research judgment. AI tools assist survey platform administration and data analysis. Practitioner primary in study design, instrument development, and validity assessment. A at C.

source_task_text: Conduct WTP studies or contingent valuation surveys
rationale: AI survey platforms + stats tools compress WTP to review-and-certify. CLD: entry-level econometric learning pathway.

source_task_text: Present valuation results to inform budget planning or policy proposals
rationale: Communicating valuation results to decision-makers requires translating economic methodology into terms that inform budget and policy choices — making assumptions transparent, representing uncertainty appropriately, and connecting results to the decision question. AI assists presentation production. A at C.

source_task_text: Present valuation results for budget/policy proposals
rationale: Presentation/defense requires professional standing.

source_task_text: Quantify services such as flood mitigation, carbon storage, or pollination
rationale: InVEST, ARIES, and similar ecosystem service modeling platforms substantially compress quantification execution once the practitioner has defined the study area, service types, and model parameterization. Practitioner contribution: configure model inputs, review outputs for plausibility given ecological knowledge of the specific landscape, interpret results. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Quantify flood mitigation, carbon storage, pollination services
rationale: Scoping requires ecological-economic integration judgment.

source_task_text: Use tools like InVEST or ARIES to model ecosystem service flows
rationale: Model execution is platform-automated once configured. Practitioner contribution: validate model spatial inputs, review flow mapping outputs against ecological expectations, troubleshoot parameterization errors. Ac at C. Lo tacit: model operation is procedural; ecological interpretation of outputs is the practitioner-primary function.

source_task_text: Use InVEST/ARIES to model ecosystem service flows
rationale: AI parameterization compresses InVEST/ARIES to review-and-certify. CLD: model operation is entry-level ES pathway.

source_task_text: Communicate ecosystem service benefits in planning or outreach materials
rationale: Communication design for ecosystem service findings requires audience calibration — what framing makes flood mitigation value legible to a county planner, carbon storage value legible to a conservation funder. AI assists visualization and document production. Practitioner primary on framing and communication design. A at C.

source_task_text: Communicate ES values for planning/investment decisions
rationale: Communication requires professional judgment re audience.

source_task_text: Develop and implement programs like conservation easements or habitat credits
rationale: Conservation easement and habitat credit program development requires integrated legal, ecological, and transactional knowledge — structuring instruments that achieve ecological outcomes while satisfying legal requirements and creating workable incentives for landowners. AI assists document drafting. A at C.

source_task_text: Develop conservation easements or habitat credit programs
rationale: Governance architecture; SC Primary. Institutional navigation irreducible.

source_task_text: Structure contracts and financial incentives to encourage stewardship on private lands
rationale: H: ARM. Contract structuring and financial incentive negotiation with private landowners requires institutional accountability and relational presence — the practitioner who negotiates the easement or stewardship agreement is the party whose professional credibility makes the transaction viable. Landowners making long-term land use decisions based on incentive structures require a trusted, accountable human counterpart.

source_task_text: Structure contracts/incentives for private land stewardship

source_task_text: Monitor compliance and ecological outcomes of enrolled properties
rationale: Compliance monitoring for conservation agreements requires site inspection, remote sensing analysis, and performance documentation. AI assists remote sensing analysis and automated documentation. Practitioner primary in site assessment and compliance determination. A at C.

source_task_text: Monitor/evaluate mechanism effectiveness and compliance
rationale: Monitoring compresses but evaluation judgment does not. A on balance.

source_task_text: Analyze how proposed projects or policies affect local jobs, income, and business activity
rationale: Economic impact analysis requires professional judgment in model selection (IMPLAN, RIMS II, custom econometric models), scope definition, and results interpretation. AI tools assist data processing and model execution. Practitioner primary on analytical design and results interpretation. A at C.

source_task_text: Analyze project/policy effects on jobs, income, business
rationale: IMPLAN execution compresses but analytical design does not. A on balance.

source_task_text: Prepare economic sections for environmental assessments or grant applications
rationale: Economic section preparation for EA/EIS documents and grant applications follows structured templates with defined analytical requirements. AI document generation tools substantially compress drafting. Practitioner contribution: ensuring analytical content meets regulatory adequacy and funder requirements. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Prepare economic sections for EAs or grant applications
rationale: NEPA econ sections follow regulatory formats. AI drafting compresses to review-and-certify. CLD HIGH: primary pathway for environmental economists.

source_task_text: Communicate economic findings to stakeholders and elected officials
rationale: H: ARM. Presenting economic findings to elected officials in official contexts — planning commission hearings, legislative briefings, agency decision meetings — constitutes institutional representation where the practitioner's credibility, professional accountability, and capacity to answer questions under scrutiny are the non-substitutable contribution. AI cannot appear before elected officials as an agency representative.

source_task_text: Communicate economic findings to stakeholders/officials
rationale: Stakeholder communication is relational-professional.

source_task_text: Measure and verify carbon sequestration from land management practices
rationale: Carbon measurement and verification requires methodological judgment (choosing appropriate allometric equations, sampling design for different vegetation types and land management contexts, uncertainty quantification). AI assists computation and documentation. Practitioner primary on measurement design and field judgment. A at C.

source_task_text: Measure/verify carbon sequestration from land management
rationale: Digital MRV compresses measurement to review-and-certify. CLD: carbon measurement is foundational learning.

source_task_text: Navigate voluntary or regulatory carbon markets for credit sales
rationale: Carbon market navigation requires integrated knowledge of registry requirements, project development protocols, verification standards, and buyer market dynamics. AI assists monitoring program design and documentation. Practitioner primary on strategic navigation and registry compliance. Hi tacit: market knowledge develops through project development experience. A at C.

source_task_text: Navigate voluntary/regulatory carbon markets for credit sales
rationale: Market navigation is SC Primary governance architecture.

source_task_text: Prepare offset documentation and reports for third-party verifiers
rationale: Third-party verification documentation follows standardized formats (ACR, VCS, CAR reporting templates). AI-assisted documentation tools substantially compress preparation. Practitioner contribution: ensuring data integrity, coordinating with verification body, addressing deficiency requests. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Prepare offset documentation for third-party verifiers
rationale: AI-drafted PDDs compress offset documentation to review-and-certify. CLD: documentation is entry-level carbon task.

source_task_text: Review policy literature and case studies to inform management strategies
rationale: ◉ S — CONFIRMED STRESS TEST CALL. AI policy research and synthesis tools (LLM-assisted literature review, AI policy database tools, automated case study compilation) execute policy literature review and case study synthesis at deployment threshold for established policy domains. Criterion 1 satisfied. P-position CLD: policy research pathway eliminated.

source_task_text: Analyze administrative and legislative proposals for environmental implications
rationale: Policy analysis for environmental implications requires professional judgment: identifying relevant analytical dimensions, assessing regulatory triggers, evaluating implementation feasibility. AI assists document review and cross-reference checking. Practitioner primary on analytical substance. A at C.

source_task_text: Summarize policy options and trade-offs in briefing documents
rationale: ◉ CLD (Moderate). AI-assisted briefing document preparation substantially compresses synthesis execution. Practitioner contribution: selecting which options to present, framing trade-offs appropriately for the decision-maker's context, ensuring political and technical accuracy. Moderate CLD: briefing writing is a developmental communication pathway for junior policy analysts.

source_task_text: Write clear and legally sound policy language for internal or public use
rationale: Policy language drafting requires legal and substantive expertise — precision in regulatory language is a professional skill where ambiguous language creates enforcement problems and litigation exposure. AI drafting tools assist; practitioner primary on legal adequacy and internal consistency. Hi tacit: policy language judgment develops through experience with regulatory interpretation disputes. A at C.

source_task_text: Review proposed policies to ensure consistency with existing frameworks
rationale: Policy consistency review requires knowledge of the full regulatory and institutional context — what existing policies say, how they have been interpreted, where there are latent tensions. AI cross-reference tools assist; practitioner primary on consistency determinations. A at C.

source_task_text: Facilitate stakeholder review of draft policies to build buy-in
rationale: H: LSD. Policy stakeholder review facilitation requires live reading of organizational and political dynamics — managing how different constituencies respond to draft language, identifying which concerns signal genuine blocking problems vs. recorded objections, and guiding deliberation toward workable consensus. The practitioner's live facilitation judgment is the non-substitutable contribution.

source_task_text: Assess how policy changes affect environmental quality, stakeholders, and operations
rationale: Regulatory impact assessment requires professional synthesis of ecological, social, and operational analysis — characterizing effects across multiple dimensions in ways that are legally defensible and analytically sound. AI assists data compilation. Practitioner primary on assessment design and cross-domain synthesis. A at C.

source_task_text: Estimate costs and benefits of alternative regulatory approaches
rationale: Cost-benefit analysis of regulatory alternatives uses standardized economic frameworks (OMB Circular A-4 methods, regulatory benefit valuation approaches) where AI tools substantially compress analytical execution. Practitioner contribution: method selection, assumption justification, uncertainty characterization for the specific regulatory context. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Prepare impact statements to support rulemaking or legislative action
rationale: Impact statement preparation follows structured regulatory documentation requirements. AI document generation tools substantially compress drafting. Practitioner contribution: ensuring analytical content meets statutory and agency adequacy requirements, coordinating review and sign-off. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Design processes for collecting and responding to public input on proposed actions
rationale: Comment process design requires professional judgment: determining appropriate comment solicitation methods for the decision context, designing response frameworks that ensure substantive comments receive substantive responses, and structuring the administrative record for legal defensibility. AI tools assist documentation. Practitioner primary on design decisions. A at C.

source_task_text: Analyze comment themes and summarize findings for decision-makers
rationale: ◉ S — CONFIRMED STRESS TEST CALL (adapted: source text T2 matches working record comment triage function). AI comment analysis and theme extraction tools (regulations.gov AI, LLM-based comment categorization, agency-specific comment analytics) are deployed in professional NEPA and rulemaking comment management. Comment volume in major actions routinely exceeds AI triage capacity. Criterion 1 satisfied for standard theme extraction and routing. P-position CLD: comment analysis pathway eliminated.

source_task_text: Maintain public transparency by publishing comment summaries and responses
rationale: Automated comment management platforms (agency e-docket systems, public notice platforms) continuously manage publication of comment summaries, response to comments documents, and administrative record maintenance. Practitioner supervises: reviews automated publications, authorizes release of response documents, ensures administrative record completeness. V at C.

source_task_text: Track environmental legislation and understand agency responsibilities
rationale: Legislative tracking platforms (LegiScan, GovTrack, Congress.gov AI monitoring, agency regulatory agenda tracking systems) continuously monitor legislative developments and flag relevant actions. Practitioner supervises: reviews flagged items, interprets implications for agency obligations, escalates significant developments to leadership. V at P: monitoring function accessible to entry-level practitioners. Lo tacit.

source_task_text: Prepare testimony, briefings, or talking points for legislative engagement
rationale: AI-assisted briefing and talking point preparation substantially compresses production of standard legislative communication formats. Practitioner contribution: ensuring substantive accuracy and political appropriateness of technical content, aligning with agency positions, adapting framing for specific legislative audiences. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Liaise with congressional staff to clarify technical aspects of proposed laws
rationale: H: ARM. Official technical liaison between agency professionals and congressional staff constitutes institutional representation — the practitioner's professional credibility, accountability, and capacity to make binding technical clarifications on behalf of the agency are the non-substitutable contribution. Congressional relationships are institutionally load-bearing.

source_task_text: Engage tribal governments early in project planning and decision-making
rationale: H: ARM. Government-to-government engagement with tribal governments is a legal obligation requiring human institutional presence and authority — the federal official who engages tribal governments in consultation is exercising the trust responsibility owed to the tribe as a sovereign government. AI cannot conduct government-to-government engagement; the relationship is definitionally between human institutional actors.

source_task_text: Facilitate government-to-government consultation meetings
rationale: H: ARM + LSD. Consultation meeting facilitation requires both institutional authority (the agency representative's presence creates the legally valid government-to-government record) and live social dynamics judgment (reading tribal leadership's concerns, ensuring consultation is meaningful rather than perfunctory). This is the paradigm H case for the ARM mechanism in Domain 6.

source_task_text: Document and incorporate tribal input into environmental and land use plans
rationale: Documentation and incorporation of tribal input requires professional judgment in characterizing concerns accurately and determining how to address them in planning documents. AI assists documentation drafting. Practitioner primary on accuracy of representation and adequacy of response. A at C.

source_task_text: Coordinate environmental management activities with other agencies to avoid duplication and conflict
rationale: Multi-agency coordination requires institutional knowledge of each agency's mandates, authorities, and organizational constraints. AI assists scheduling and communication logistics. Practitioner primary on coordination design and conflict resolution. A at C.

source_task_text: Participate in interagency workgroups or task forces
rationale: H: ARM. Official participation in interagency workgroups requires institutional representation — the practitioner's statements in official interagency proceedings constitute agency positions. Workgroup participation builds the relational infrastructure for effective interagency coordination; AI cannot build these institutional relationships.

source_task_text: Align timelines and data standards across jurisdictions for shared projects
rationale: Cross-jurisdictional timeline and standard alignment requires knowledge of each jurisdiction's constraints and institutional authority to negotiate accommodations. AI assists project tracking and document management. Practitioner primary on negotiation and commitment-making. A at C.

source_task_text: Draft memoranda of understanding (MOUs) or interagency agreements for shared responsibilities
rationale: MOU and interagency agreement drafting requires sophisticated knowledge of each agency's authorities, limitations, and organizational constraints. AI drafting tools assist; practitioner primary on legal adequacy and institutional workability. Hi tacit: agreement development requires deep knowledge of interagency relationship history. A at C.

source_task_text: Define roles, resource commitments, and protocols for joint initiatives
rationale: H: ARM. Defining and committing organizational resources and roles in interagency agreements requires institutional authority — the practitioner who negotiates these commitments is binding their organization in ways that create ongoing obligations. AI cannot exercise organizational authority or commit institutional resources.

source_task_text: Monitor agreement implementation and update as needed
rationale: Agreement implementation monitoring and periodic update requires institutional knowledge and relationship maintenance with partner agencies. AI assists tracking and documentation. Practitioner primary on compliance assessment and renegotiation. A at C.

source_task_text: Lead planning efforts that span watershed or ecosystem boundaries
rationale: H: ARM. Cross-jurisdictional planning leadership requires institutional authority to convene partner agencies and commit the lead agency to a shared planning process. The leader's professional credibility and institutional position determine whether other jurisdictions engage substantively. This is a governance convening function AI cannot perform.

source_task_text: Harmonize regulatory requirements and priorities across jurisdictions
rationale: Regulatory harmonization requires multi-jurisdictional legal knowledge and institutional negotiation. AI assists cross-document analysis and gap identification. Practitioner primary on harmonization determinations and negotiating accommodations between incompatible requirements. A at C.

source_task_text: Facilitate multi-jurisdictional stakeholder engagement processes
rationale: H: LSD + ARM. Multi-jurisdictional stakeholder facilitation requires live management of group dynamics across jurisdictional interests — different agencies, communities, and governments with competing claims and legitimacy questions. The practitioner's live facilitation judgment and institutional standing are both essential.

source_task_text: Support implementation of global agreements like the Convention on Biological Diversity
rationale: International agreement implementation support requires knowledge of treaty obligations, reporting requirements, and domestic implementation frameworks. AI assists documentation and compliance tracking. Practitioner primary on implementation strategy and coordination. A at C.

source_task_text: Coordinate with international partners on cross-border habitat management
rationale: H: ARM. International coordination requires institutional representation — the practitioner coordinating with foreign agency counterparts is exercising diplomatic and technical authority on behalf of their organization. Cross-border habitat management partnerships are built on relational trust between institutional actors.

source_task_text: Contribute data and reports to meet treaty or bilateral agreement obligations
rationale: Treaty reporting and data contribution follows standardized formats (CBD national reports, CITES trade data, Ramsar information sheets). AI-assisted documentation tools compress preparation. Practitioner contribution: ensuring data quality and accuracy of national reporting, coordinating internal review and authorization. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Conduct greenhouse gas inventories for organizations, projects, or jurisdictions
rationale: GHG accounting software platforms (Persefoni, Watershed, Salesforce Net Zero Cloud, EPA GHGRP reporting tools) substantially automate inventory calculation from input data. Practitioner contribution: ensuring input data quality, reviewing outputs for plausibility, interpreting results for disclosure and reduction planning. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Quantify carbon sequestration from land management or conservation activities
rationale: Sequestration quantification requires ecological and methodological judgment in addition to calculation tools — selecting appropriate allometric equations, accounting for uncertainty, handling non-standard vegetation types. AI assists computation. Practitioner primary on methodological design and field data collection. A at C.

source_task_text: Develop monitoring and verification plans for carbon accounting
rationale: MRV framework design requires specialized knowledge of registry protocols, measurement uncertainty standards, and verification requirements for specific land management and project types. AI assists documentation. Practitioner primary on framework design. Horizon 2: MRV standards developing rapidly for nature-based solutions. A at C.

source_task_text: Develop biodiversity credit methodologies quantifying conservation outcomes
rationale: Biodiversity credit methodology development requires ecological expertise, legal knowledge of mitigation requirements, and understanding of credit buyer needs. AI assists literature review and documentation. Practitioner primary on methodology design. Horizon 2: biodiversity credit market methodologies are actively developing with regulatory evolution. A at C.

source_task_text: Establish or participate in habitat mitigation banks or conservation banks
rationale: H: ARM. Banking instrument establishment requires institutional authority — the landowner, conservation organization, or agency that establishes a mitigation bank is creating a regulatory instrument that generates credits with legal standing. The banking approval process involves formal government-to-government regulatory negotiation that AI cannot conduct.

source_task_text: Facilitate biodiversity credit transactions between buyers and sellers
rationale: H: ARM. Credit transaction facilitation in a regulatory mitigation context requires institutional accountability — both buyer and seller need a credible, accountable professional to ensure the transaction satisfies regulatory requirements and is properly documented in the mitigation tracking system. The facilitator's professional credibility is load-bearing.

source_task_text: Broker transactions between environmental credit buyers and sellers
rationale: H: ARM. Environmental credit brokerage involves fiduciary and relational accountability — buyers and sellers of regulatory instruments require a credible, accountable professional counterpart whose professional reputation is at stake in each transaction. This is not purely information-based exchange; it is a trust-based institutional relationship.

source_task_text: Evaluate quality and pricing of environmental credits
rationale: Credit quality and pricing evaluation requires domain expertise in ecological outcomes, registry standards, and market dynamics. AI assists price comparison and registry data review. Practitioner primary on quality assessment judgment. A at C.

source_task_text: Navigate registries, exchanges, and market platforms for credit trading
rationale: Carbon and biodiversity registry platforms (Verra Registry, ACR, CBDM) continuously manage account balances, credit issuances, and transaction records. Practitioner supervises account management: reviews automated notifications, initiates authorized transactions, monitors registry compliance. V at C.

source_task_text: Design payment for ecosystem services (PES) programs
rationale: PES program design requires integrated ecological and financial expertise — structuring payments that provide sufficient incentives for land management change while being tied to verifiable ecological outcomes. AI assists economic modeling and documentation. Practitioner primary on program design. Horizon 2: PES mechanisms continue to evolve with carbon and biodiversity market development. A at C.

source_task_text: Develop conservation financing structures (green bonds, conservation funds, impact investments)
rationale: Conservation financing structure development requires sophisticated financial and legal expertise. AI assists documentation and financial modeling. Practitioner primary on structure design and legal compliance. Horizon 2: novel conservation financing instruments actively developing. A at C.

source_task_text: Build partnerships between conservation providers and beneficiaries
rationale: H: ARM + LSD. Conservation partnership development requires sustained relational presence and institutional trust-building — the conservation professional who builds a relationship with a downstream beneficiary is creating the institutional foundation for a payment relationship. Partnership building is definitionally a human relational act.

source_task_text: Structure green bond issuances for environmental projects
rationale: Green bond structuring requires specialized financial expertise and legal knowledge of green bond frameworks. AI assists documentation and compliance checking. Practitioner primary on structure design and investor communication. Horizon 2: green bond market standards and instruments continuing to develop. A at C.

source_task_text: Evaluate environmental credentials and impact of green investments
rationale: Environmental impact evaluation requires professional judgment in assessing additionality, permanence, and ecological outcome quality of green investment claims. AI assists data compilation and ESG metric analysis. Practitioner primary on assessment judgment. A at C.

source_task_text: Ensure compliance with green bond principles and standards
rationale: Compliance verification against Green Bond Principles, Climate Bonds Standard, and ICMA frameworks follows structured checklists that AI tools substantially automate. Practitioner contribution: reviewing compliance determinations, addressing exceptions, authorizing compliance documentation. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Conduct exposure assessments for environmental contaminants
rationale: Exposure assessment requires technical judgment: selecting appropriate exposure scenarios, accounting for sensitive populations, handling data gaps, and applying conservative assumptions consistently with regulatory guidance. AI assists calculation. Practitioner primary on design and interpretation. A at C.

source_task_text: Calculate health risks from environmental exposures using standard methods
rationale: Health risk calculation using EPA standard methods (cancer slope factors, reference doses, exposure factor handbooks) is substantially automated by risk assessment software platforms. Practitioner contribution: method selection, assumption documentation, and results interpretation for the specific contaminant and population context. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Communicate health risk findings to affected communities and decision-makers
rationale: H: LSD + ARM. Community health risk communication requires live presence and trust — explaining cancer risk findings, addressing community anxiety, maintaining transparency about uncertainty, and responding to community concerns in real time. Risk communication in environmental health contexts has direct bearing on community health decisions; the practitioner's live presence and responsiveness are the non-substitutable contribution.

source_task_text: Use environmental justice screening tools (EJSCREEN, CalEnviroScreen) to identify overburdened communities
rationale: EJ screening tool platforms (EJSCREEN, CalEnviroScreen, Justice40) continuously maintain and update community burden indicators and generate screening reports from geographic queries. Practitioner supervises: runs screening queries for specific areas, reviews outputs for completeness, contextualizes automated screening results. V at P: screening platform operation accessible to entry-level practitioners. Lo tacit.

source_task_text: Conduct environmental justice analyses for projects and policies
rationale: EJ analysis for projects and policies requires professional judgment integrating screening tool outputs with community engagement findings, cumulative impact assessment, and regulatory requirements. AI assists data compilation. Practitioner primary on analytical synthesis and equity framing. A at C.

source_task_text: Engage environmental justice communities meaningfully in decision-making
rationale: H: LSD. EJ community engagement requires live presence and trust — entering communities that have historically experienced environmental harm and institutional betrayal, facilitating authentic participation, and ensuring that engagement is substantive rather than procedural. The practitioner's live cultural competence and relational accountability are the non-substitutable contribution. ⚑ Delphi: L1 ethical lens — equity obligations for overburdened communities.

source_task_text: Co-design research projects with community partners
rationale: H: ARM + LSD. Community co-design requires sustained relational presence and genuine shared authority — the practitioner who co-designs research with community partners is entering an accountability relationship where the community's research priorities and analytical frameworks have equal standing. AI cannot participate in this co-governance relationship.

source_task_text: Build community capacity for data collection and interpretation
rationale: H: ARM. Community capacity building requires sustained relational presence — the practitioner builds the community's technical capability through relationship, trust, and responsive pedagogy over time. This is a form of professional accountability to community partners that AI cannot substitute.

source_task_text: Ensure research findings are accessible and actionable for communities
rationale: H: LSD. Making research findings actionable for communities requires live engagement — presenting findings in community settings, responding to community interpretation, and facilitating community-owned sense-making of results. The practitioner's presence in community spaces and responsiveness to community questions are essential to the CBPR accountability framework.

source_task_text: Evaluate toxicity of environmental contaminants
rationale: Toxicity evaluation requires professional judgment: interpreting dose-response relationships, assessing data quality, selecting appropriate toxicological endpoints. AI assists literature review and database queries. Practitioner primary on evaluation judgment and uncertainty characterization. A at C.

source_task_text: Assess exposure pathways for chemicals in air, water, soil, and food
rationale: Exposure pathway assessment requires professional judgment: constructing site-specific conceptual site models, identifying complete exposure pathways, and characterizing pathway completeness against regulatory standards. AI assists database queries and modeling. A at C.

source_task_text: Identify vulnerable populations and exposure scenarios
rationale: Vulnerable population identification requires professional judgment integrating epidemiological knowledge, site-specific demographics, and regulatory sensitivity standards. AI assists demographic data compilation. Practitioner primary on vulnerability characterization and its implications for risk characterization. A at C.

source_task_text: Monitor air pollutant concentrations and assess compliance with standards
rationale: Air quality monitoring networks (EPA AQS, state monitoring platforms, continuous emissions monitoring systems) continuously monitor pollutant concentrations and generate compliance status reports. Practitioner supervises: reviews automated compliance reports, investigates exceedances, coordinates with regulated entities on corrective action. V at C. Lo tacit: monitoring platform operation is procedural; compliance investigation is A-adjacent.

source_task_text: Develop air quality improvement plans and emission reduction strategies
rationale: Air quality improvement planning requires integrated technical, regulatory, and community knowledge — designing emission reduction strategies that achieve NAAQS attainment while addressing EJ concerns and maintaining economic viability. AI assists modeling. Practitioner primary on plan design. Horizon 2: modeling and planning tools actively developing. A at C.

source_task_text: Evaluate health impacts of air pollution on communities
rationale: Community health impact evaluation requires professional judgment integrating air quality modeling, epidemiological methods, and health outcome characterization. AI assists modeling. Practitioner primary on impact assessment design and results interpretation. A at C.

source_task_text: Identify appropriate climate finance sources for projects (GCF, GEF, bilateral, private)
rationale: ◉ S. AI climate finance landscape tools and LLM-assisted funder matching now execute climate finance source identification for standard project types at deployment threshold. Matching project characteristics (sector, geography, stage, implementing entity) to funder profiles is an information-intensive task that AI substantially automates. P-position CLD: climate finance research pathway compressed.

source_task_text: Identify climate finance sources (GCF, GEF, bilateral, private)
rationale: AI funding databases compress scanning to review-and-certify. CLD: scanning is entry-level.

source_task_text: Develop proposals for climate finance from public and private sources
rationale: Climate finance proposal development requires strategic judgment and stakeholder knowledge — understanding funder priorities, structuring proposals to demonstrate climate additionality, and building the political relationships that advance applications through competitive review processes. AI assists drafting. Practitioner primary on strategic design. A at C.

source_task_text: Develop proposals for climate finance
rationale: Prescribed formats (GCF notes, GEF PIFs). LLM compresses to review-and-certify. CLD HIGH: primary entry to climate finance.

source_task_text: Structure blended finance approaches combining grants, loans, and equity
rationale: Blended finance structuring requires highly specialized financial and legal expertise extending well beyond standard environmental management career progression. X: this is advanced specialist work. Horizon 2: blended finance instruments for climate are actively developing. AI assists financial modeling. A at X.

source_task_text: Structure blended finance (grants, loans, equity)
rationale: Senior-specialist governance architecture. Resists compression.

source_task_text: Structure green or climate bond issuances for climate projects
rationale: Climate bond structuring requires specialized expertise in capital markets, climate finance standards, and regulatory compliance. X: specialist function. AI assists documentation. A at X.

source_task_text: Structure green/climate bond issuances
rationale: Bond structuring is governance architecture. Institutional judgment dominates.

source_task_text: Ensure compliance with Climate Bonds Standard and green bond principles
rationale: Climate Bonds Standard and ICMA Green Bond Principles compliance verification follows structured frameworks that AI compliance checking tools substantially automate. Practitioner contribution: reviewing compliance determinations, managing exceptions, authorizing reporting. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Ensure compliance with CBI Standard and green bond principles
rationale: Automated compliance verification compresses to review-and-certify. CLD: standards checking is entry-level.

source_task_text: Prepare climate impact reports for bond investors
rationale: Climate impact reporting for bond investors follows standardized formats (post-issuance reporting templates, green bond impact reporting frameworks). AI-assisted reporting tools substantially compress preparation. Practitioner contribution: ensuring data quality and investor-appropriate framing. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Prepare climate impact reports for bond investors
rationale: ICMA template + AI aggregation compress reporting to review-and-certify. CLD: impact reporting is entry-level.

source_task_text: Navigate compliance carbon markets (cap-and-trade, carbon taxes)
rationale: Compliance market navigation requires regulatory and strategic expertise — understanding allowance allocation, compliance period management, banking and borrowing rules, and offset procurement strategies in specific market jurisdictions. AI assists monitoring and analysis. Practitioner primary on strategy. A at C.

source_task_text: Navigate compliance carbon markets (cap-and-trade)
rationale: Compliance market navigation is SC Primary governance architecture.

source_task_text: Develop carbon offset projects for voluntary markets
rationale: Offset project development requires integrated ecological, legal, and market knowledge. AI assists documentation and monitoring design. Practitioner primary on project design and registry compliance. Horizon 2: voluntary carbon market standards actively evolving. A at C.

source_task_text: Develop carbon offset projects for voluntary markets
rationale: Delphi: Borderline Ac. PDD drafting compresses but development judgment keeps A.

source_task_text: Evaluate carbon market regulations and trading opportunities
rationale: Carbon market regulatory evaluation requires specialized knowledge of market design and regulatory evolution across jurisdictions. AI assists monitoring and analysis. Practitioner primary on strategic interpretation. A at C.

source_task_text: Evaluate carbon market regulations and trading opportunities
rationale: Regulatory evaluation is judgment-intensive governance work.

source_task_text: Identify adaptation finance sources and develop funding proposals
rationale: Adaptation finance source identification and proposal development for standard adaptation categories (coastal resilience, water security, heat action plans) increasingly AI-assisted through funder matching tools and AI proposal drafting. Practitioner contribution: strategic framing, relationship cultivation, adaptation rationale development. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Identify adaptation finance sources and develop proposals
rationale: Scanning + proposal drafting both meet Ac (parallel 6.8.1). CLD: combined compression.

source_task_text: Demonstrate adaptation rationale and benefits in project design
rationale: Adaptation rationale development requires professional judgment in linking climate risk analysis to project design choices and articulating climate-proofing logic for funder audiences. AI assists documentation. Practitioner primary. Horizon 2: adaptation benefit assessment frameworks developing. A at C.

source_task_text: Demonstrate adaptation rationale and benefits in design
rationale: Adaptation rationale requires site-specific vulnerability judgment.

source_task_text: Monitor and report adaptation outcomes for funders
rationale: Adaptation outcome monitoring and reporting follows structured M&E frameworks required by climate funders. AI-assisted monitoring tools and reporting platforms substantially compress reporting cycles. Practitioner contribution: data quality assurance and funder relationship management. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Monitor and report adaptation outcomes for funders
rationale: Automated M&E compress reporting to review-and-certify. CLD: entry-level M&E pathway.

source_task_text: Assess physical and transition risks from climate change on investments
rationale: Climate risk assessment requires professional judgment: selecting appropriate physical and transition risk scenarios, applying TCFD framework to specific investment types, and characterizing risk materiality. AI assists scenario modeling and data analysis. Practitioner primary on risk characterization. A at C.

source_task_text: Assess physical/transition climate risks on investments
rationale: AI risk platforms compress TCFD assessment to review-and-certify. CLD: climate risk data collection is entry-level.

source_task_text: Develop climate risk disclosure and reporting frameworks
rationale: Climate risk disclosure frameworks (TCFD-aligned, SEC climate disclosure, ISSB standards) follow structured templates that AI tools substantially automate for standard investment categories. Practitioner contribution: ensuring disclosure adequacy, legal review coordination, stakeholder communication. Ac at C.

source_task_text: Develop climate risk disclosure/reporting frameworks
rationale: Disclosure framework design is governance architecture (SEC, ISSB, TCFD).

source_task_text: Integrate climate risk into investment decision-making
rationale: Climate risk integration into investment decisions requires professional judgment combining financial analysis, physical risk science, and transition risk assessment — determining how climate risk affects investment thesis, expected returns, and portfolio strategy. AI assists analysis. Practitioner primary on integration judgment. Horizon 2: climate risk investment frameworks actively developing. A at C.

source_task_text: Integrate climate risk into investment decision-making
rationale: Senior-specialist: fiduciary judgment and institutional authority.

Identify and document situations where institutional pressures conflict with obligations to produce honest regulatory findings
Apply professional codes of ethics and scientific integrity standards to regulatory contexts (conflict disclosure, uncertainty, dissenting views)

Design human-in-the-loop oversight architectures defining practitioner roles, escalation triggers, and accountability pathways

Evaluate AI-generated species identifications, habitat assessments, or ecological predictions against field observations and established ecological knowledge
Assess AI-assisted regulatory analyses against applicable legal standards and regulatory interpretive guidance
Document validation findings and communicate the basis and confidence level of validation judgments to decision-makers
Analyze an AI-augmented workflow to identify which entry-level formation tasks have been compressed by automation and what tacit knowledge practitioners are no longer developing
Design deliberate practice sequences, mentoring structures, and staged exposure protocols that rebuild development pathways compressed by AI adoption
Evaluate whether redesigned workflows are producing intended formation outcomes and revise in response to observed gaps
